summary.en: Following the 'Rites of Zhou', Wang Mang restored the ancient official title 'Xihe', granting it significant economic powers such as overseeing the Five Equalisations and Six Controls. Xihe was originally a celestial official under Emperor Yao. Through this, Wang Mang sought historical legitimacy for his 'reforms by entrusting antiquity'. The establishment of Xihe laid the inst

statement.zh: 王莽依据《周礼》恢复"羲和"古官名，赋予其监督五均六筦等经济大权。羲和原是尧帝的天文官，王莽借此为其"托古改制"寻求历史合法性。羲和的设立为后续王莽全面推行经济管制措施铺垫了制度基础。
statement.en:
Following the 'Rites of Zhou', Wang Mang restored the ancient official title 'Xihe', granting it significant economic powers such as overseeing the Five Equalisations and Six Controls. Xihe was originally a celestial official under Emperor Yao. Through this, Wang Mang sought historical legitimacy for his 'reforms by entrusting antiquity'. The establishment of Xihe laid the institutional groundwork for Wang Mang's subsequent comprehensive implementation of economic control measures.

For Asia in 1 CE, “Wang Mang Established the Office of Xihe” is a traceable node of Politics change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Wang Mang Plotted to Make His Daughter Empress

summary.en: To further consolidate his power, Wang Mang planned to marry his daughter to Emperor Ping of Han. He first had his confidants propose establishing an empress, then feigned modesty. Eventually, under public 'petition', the Grand Empress Dowager issued an edict making the Wang daughter empress, greatly enhancing his status as a consort kin.

statement.zh: 王莽为进一步巩固权力，策划将女儿嫁给汉平帝为皇后。他先指使亲信提议立后，又假意谦让，最终在群臣“请愿”下太皇太后下诏立王氏女为后，大大增强其外戚地位。

title.en: Ovid Completed 'Metamorphoses'

summary.en: The Roman poet Ovid completed his narrative poem 'Metamorphoses', telling over 250 Greco-Roman myths from the creation of the world to the deification of Julius Caesar, centering on the theme of 'transformation'. With its exquisite narrative and beautiful language, it became a classic of Latin literature, profoundly influencing later European literature and art.

title.en: Wang Mang Declared 'Acting Emperor' and Changed Era to Jushe

summary.en: In AD 6, after poisoning Emperor Ping, Wang Mang installed the two-year-old Ruzi Ying as crown prince, declared himself 'Jia Huangdi' (Acting Emperor), and changed the era name to Jushe. Court officials addressed him as 'She Huangdi' (Regent Emperor). He used imperial ritual in sacrifices and court assemblies, with power equal to that of a true emperor. This was one of the most

statement.zh: 公元6年，汉平帝被王莽毒杀后，王莽立两岁孺子刘婴为太子，自称假皇帝（代理皇帝），改年号为居摄。朝臣称其为摄皇帝，在祭祀和朝会中使用皇帝礼仪，权力已等同于真正皇帝。这是王莽篡汉过程中最关键的步骤之一。
statement.en:
In AD 6, after poisoning Emperor Ping, Wang Mang installed the two-year-old Ruzi Ying as crown prince, declared himself 'Jia Huangdi' (Acting Emperor), and changed the era name to Jushe. Court officials addressed him as 'She Huangdi' (Regent Emperor). He used imperial ritual in sacrifices and court assemblies, with power equal to that of a true emperor. This was one of the most crucial steps in Wang Mang's path to usurpation.

For Asia in 6 CE, “Wang Mang Declared 'Acting Emperor' and Changed Era to Jushe” is a traceable node of Politics change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Liu Chong's Revolt Against Wang Mang Failed

summary.en: Liu Chong, a member of the Han imperial clan, raised troops in Nanyang to attack Wang Mang. Although he gained some support from other Liu clan members and officials, his forces were insufficient and he was quickly suppressed. This was the first open armed action against Wang Mang.

statement.zh:
汉宗室刘崇在南阳起兵讨伐王莽，虽得到部分刘氏宗族和官僚支持，但兵力不足迅速被镇压。这是第一次公开的反莽武装行动。起兵以宗室名望为号召，仓促集结、缺乏后援；官府迅速调兵，将其各个击破。反抗的火种却由此传开。

把「刘崇起兵反莽失败」放回公元6年的西汉，可以看到军事变化的一个具体切面。

title.en: Wang Mang Enfeoffed Imperial Clan to Appease the Liu Family

summary.en: In AD 6, while acting as acting emperor, Wang Mang enfeoffed numerous Liu imperial clan members and descendants of meritorious officials to win support and appease those dissatisfied with his usurpation. title.en: Augustus Established the Military Treasury

summary.en: Roman Emperor Augustus established the 'aerarium militare' (military treasury) to specifically pay pensions and land compensation to retired soldiers. Its funding sources included a 5% inheritance tax and a 1% auction sales tax, ensuring the army's loyalty to the emperor.

statement.zh: 罗马皇帝奥古斯都设立军事财库（aerarium militare），专门支付退役军人的养老金和土地补偿金，资金来源包括5%继承税和1%拍卖税，确保了军队对皇帝的忠诚。
statement.en:
Roman Emperor Augustus established the 'aerarium militare' (military treasury) to specifically pay pensions and land compensation to retired soldiers. Its funding sources included a 5% inheritance tax and a 1% auction sales tax, ensuring the army's loyalty to the emperor.

title.en: Panicked Wang Mang Wrote a Prayer to Heaven

summary.en: Faced with the anti-Wang Mang wave led by Zhai Yi, Zhao Ming, Huo Hong, and others, Wang Mang became distraught. He wrote a prayer and proclamation to Heaven professing his loyalty, reflecting his growing reliance on superstitious means to stabilize people's hearts.

statement.zh:
面对翟义、赵明、霍鸿等反莽浪潮，王莽惶恐不安，撰写告天文策向上天表白忠心，反映其愈发依赖迷信手段稳定人心。起兵与流言动摇新朝合法性，告天把政治危机转化为天命叙事；符命与谶纬成为统治工具。以神道自证的做法未能阻止反抗蔓延。

title.en: Zhai Yi Revolted, Made Liu Xin Emperor

summary.en: The Prefect of Dong Commandery, Zhai Yi, raised troops against Wang Mang in Henan, installing a descendant of the Han imperial house, Liu Xin, as the Son of Heaven. He issued a proclamation calling on the realm to attack Wang Mang, and his forces quickly swelled to over one hundred thousand men.

statement.zh: 东郡太守翟义在河南起兵反莽，立汉宗室后裔刘信为天子，发布檄文号召天下讨伐王莽，队伍迅速发展到十余万人。檄文以恢复汉室为号召，联合地方豪强与郡国兵，形成对新朝合法性的一次公开挑战；起兵虽被镇压，却鼓舞了各地反抗。它以宗室为旗帜，把地方不满转为政治动员。

statement.zh: 公元7年，王莽派王邑、孙建等率军镇压了翟义和刘信的起兵。翟义在陈留一带聚众十余万，声势浩大。王邑采用分进合击战术，在圉县（今河南杞县）击败翟义军。翟义兵败被俘后处死。此战的胜利消除了王莽篡位道路上最大的军事威胁。
statement.en:
In AD 7, Wang Mang sent Wang Yi, Sun Jian, and others to suppress the revolt of Zhai Yi and Liu Xin. Zhai Yi had assembled over 100,000 men in Chenliu, creating a powerful force. Wang Yi employed a tactic of converging columns and launched a surprise attack, defeating Zhai Yi's army at Yuxian (modern-day Qixian, Henan). Zhai Yi was captured and executed. This victory eliminated the greatest military threat to Wang Mang's path to usurpation.

For Asia in 7 CE, “Wang Yi et al. Decisively Defeated Zhai Yi's Army” is a traceable node of Military change whose significance is best read through later events.

statement.en:
In AD 8, after formally declaring himself emperor and establishing the Xin dynasty, Wang Mang deposed Ruzi Liu Ying, granting him the title 'Duke of Ding'an'. Liu Ying was confined to a specific residence, his family forbidden from communicating with him. When Liu Ying grew up, he could not even distinguish the six domestic animals. Wang Mang kept Liu clan members under strict surveillance, and the Western Han imperial house completely lost power.

title.en: Augustus Conducted a Roman Census

summary.en: Roman Emperor Augustus conducted an empire-wide census, counting the number and property of citizens, recording the results in the 'Res Gestae Divi Augusti' (Deeds of the Divine Augustus), providing a basis for taxation and military conscription.

statement.zh:
罗马皇帝奥古斯都进行帝国人口普查，统计公民数量及财产状况，结果登记于《功业录》中，为税收和军事征调提供依据。普查以户籍与财产评估为基础，行省与城市配合登记；数据用于征税、征兵与福利分配。统计把帝国治理推向制度化。

把「奥古斯都进行罗马人口普查」放回公元8年的罗马帝国，可以看到政治变化的一个具体切面。

summary.en: Vonones I ascended the Parthian throne with the support of the Parthian nobility. Having lived as a hostage in Rome for many years, he was deeply influenced by Roman culture. summary.en: Egypt, as the 'breadbasket of Rome', shipped about 20 million modii (approximately 120 million liters) of wheat from Alexandria to Rome annually, feeding hundreds of thousands of commoners receiving free grain rations. title.en: Wang Mang Implemented Currency Reforms

summary.en: Wang Mang carried out currency reforms, minting new coin types such as large coins, inscribed knife coins, and inscribed 'wrong' knife coins. The chaotic currency system and currency devaluation severely impacted the civilian economy, leading to soaring prices and hardship for both farmers and merchants, becoming an important reason for the rapid collapse of the Xin dynasty.

statement.zh:
王莽进行货币改革，铸造大钱、契刀、错刀等新币种，币制混乱、货币贬值，民间经济受严重冲击，物价飞涨、农商俱困，成为新朝迅速崩溃的重要原因。新币名目繁多、比值失当，旧钱屡禁不止，交易与赋税折算无所适从；民间私铸与盗铸盛行，官府严刑亦不能止。

把「王莽推行币制改革」放回公元9年的新朝，可以看到经济变化的一个具体切面。
statement.en: Wang Mang carried out currency reforms, minting new coins such as the large coin, the inscribed knife and the wrong knife; the chaotic system and depreciation hit the civilian economy, prices soared, farmers and merchants alike suffered, and this became a major cause of the Xin dynasty's rapid collapse.

zh: 王莽进行货币改革，铸造大钱、契刀、错刀等新币种，币制混乱、货币贬值，民间经济受严重冲击，物价飞涨、农商俱困，成为新朝迅速崩溃的重要原因。新币名目繁多、比值失当，旧钱屡禁不止，交易与赋税折算无所适从；民间私铸与盗铸盛行，官府严刑亦不能止。
王莽进行货币改革，铸造大钱、契刀、错刀等新币种，币制混乱、货币贬值，民间经济受严重冲击，物价飞涨、农商俱困，成为新朝迅速崩溃的重要原因。
en: Wang Mang carried out currency reforms, minting new coins such as the large coin, the inscribed knife and the wrong knife; the chaotic system and depreciation hit the civilian economy, prices soared, farmers and merchants alike suffered, and this became a major cause of the Xin dynasty's rapid collapse.

Families with fewer than eight members could not own more than one 'jing' (a unit of land area), with excess to be distributed among clan members and neighbors. Aimed at solving land annexation, the decree was strongly resisted by powerful fam

statement.en: Wang Mang issued the 'Wangtian Decree', declaring all land nationwide state-owned and renamed 'Wangtian', forbidding buying and selling.

zh: 王莽颁布“王田令”，宣布全国土地收归国有更名“王田”，禁止买卖。

title.en: Banned the Buying and Selling of Slaves

summary.en: Wang Mang issued a decree prohibiting the buying and selling of slaves nationwide, reflecting the Confucian principle of benevolence that 'human nature is the most precious'. However, powerful local families strongly resisted, making enforcement difficult, and the ban ultimately proved ineffectual.

statement.zh: 王莽颁布法令禁止全国买卖奴婢，体现“天地之性人为贵”的儒家仁政思想。
statement.en: Wang Mang issued a decree prohibiting the buying and selling of slaves nationwide, reflecting the Confucian principle of benevolence that 'human nature is the most precious'.

zh: 王莽颁布法令禁止全国买卖奴婢，体现“天地之性人为贵”的儒家仁政思想。
en: Wang Mang issued a decree prohibiting the buying and selling of slaves nationwide, reflecting the Confucian principle of benevolence that 'human nature is the most precious'.

title.en: Wang Mang Reformed Official Titles and Ranks

summary.en: After formally declaring himself emperor, Wang Mang undertook a large-scale reform of the official system and noble ranks based on the 'Rites of Zhou': establishing Four Assistants, Three Dukes, Four Generals at the center, changing many local commandery and county names to ancient titles, and dividing noble ranks into five grades: Gong, Hou, Bo, Zi, Nan. These antiquarian refo

statement.zh: 王莽正式称帝后，依照《周礼》大规模改革官制爵位：中央设四辅、三公、四将，地方郡县大量改为古称，爵位分公侯伯子男五等。
statement.en: After formally declaring himself emperor, Wang Mang undertook a large-scale reform of the official system and noble ranks based on the 'Rites of Zhou': establishing Four Assistants, Three Dukes, Four Generals at the center, changing many local commandery and county names to ancient titles, and dividing noble ranks into five grades: Gong, Hou, Bo, Zi, Nan.

zh: 王莽正式称帝后，依照《周礼》大规模改革官制爵位：中央设四辅、三公、四将，地方郡县大量改为古称，爵位分公侯伯子男五等。
en: After formally declaring himself emperor, Wang Mang undertook a large-scale reform of the official system and noble ranks based on the 'Rites of Zhou': establishing Four Assistants, Three Dukes, Four Generals at the center, changing many local commandery and county names to ancient titles, and dividing noble ranks into five grades: Gong, Hou, Bo, Zi, Nan.

title.en: The Battle of the Teutoburg Forest: Rome stops east of the Rhine

summary.en: In the autumn of 9 CE Arminius and his Germanic followers ambushed Varus's three legions in the Teutoburg Forest; the fighting lasted four days and nearly 20,000 Romans were killed. Rome then stopped trying to conquer Germania east of the Rhine and garrisoned the frontier with at least eight legions. Augustus's grief is reported by Suetonius, a later biographer.

statement.zh: 公元9年秋，阿尔米尼乌斯率日耳曼部众在条顿堡森林伏击普布利乌斯·昆克提利乌斯·瓦鲁斯率领的三个罗马军团。战斗持续四天，三个军团被歼灭。
statement.en: In the autumn of 9 CE, Arminius and his Germanic followers ambushed three Roman legions under Publius Quinctilius Varus in the Teutoburg Forest. The fighting lasted four days, and all three legions were destroyed.

sources.locator: Britannica, Battle of the Teutoburg Forest, opening paragraph
sources.excerpt: The Battle of the Teutoburg Forest occurred in the autumn of 9 CE when Arminius, a German tribal leader, organized ambushes on three Roman legions led by Publius Quinctilius Varus. Over four days, Arminius and his insurgents destroyed all three legions, which stopped Rome from conquering Germania east of the Rhine River.

zh: 公元9年秋，阿尔米尼乌斯率日耳曼部众在条顿堡森林伏击普布利乌斯·昆克提利乌斯·瓦鲁斯率领的三个罗马军团。
战斗持续四天，三个军团被歼灭。
en: In the autumn of 9 CE, Arminius and his Germanic followers ambushed three Roman legions under Publius Quinctilius Varus in the Teutoburg Forest.
The fighting lasted four days, and all three legions were destroyed.

note.zh: 日期、伏击者、三个军团与四天战斗照条目写。
note.en: Date, attacker, three legions and four days follow the entry.

statement.zh: 瓦鲁斯是日耳曼地区的总督，统率第17、18、19军团；阿尔米尼乌斯是切鲁西部落贵族，组织了这次伏击。
statement.en: Varus was governor of Germania and commanded the 17th, 18th and 19th legions; Arminius was a Cherusci noble who organized the ambush.

sources.locator: Britannica, Battle of the Teutoburg Forest, paragraph 2
sources.excerpt: In the meantime, Publius Quinctilius Varus acted as governor of the proto-province of Germania. He had command of the three legions constituting the army of Germania Inferior: Legio XVII, Legio XVIII, and Legio XIX.

zh: 瓦鲁斯是日耳曼地区的总督，统率第17、18、19军团；阿尔米尼乌斯是切鲁西部落贵族，组织了这次伏击。
en: Varus was governor of Germania and commanded the 17th, 18th and 19th legions; Arminius was a Cherusci noble who organized the ambush.

note.zh: 军团编号照条目；不写辅助部队精确人数。
note.en: Legion numbers follow the entry; no exact auxiliary count.

statement.zh: 罗马方面近20,000人阵亡，日耳曼方损失很小。
statement.en: Nearly 20,000 Romans were killed, while German losses were minimal.

sources.locator: Britannica, Battle of the Teutoburg Forest, paragraph 3
sources.excerpt: In total, nearly 20,000 Romans were killed in the engagement, while German losses were minimal.

zh: 罗马方面近20,000人阵亡，日耳曼方损失很小。
en: Nearly 20,000 Romans were killed, while German losses were minimal.

note.zh: 伤亡为条目估计，不写“一个不剩”。
note.en: Casualties are the entry's estimates; no claim that none escaped.

statement.zh: 战后，提比略又对日耳曼部落发动三次战役，但选择不占领莱茵河以东的土地，而是在边境驻扎至少八个军团。
statement.en: After the battle, Tiberius waged three more campaigns against the Germanic tribes, but chose not to occupy their land east of the Rhine and stationed at least eight legions on the frontier.

sources.locator: Britannica, Battle of the Teutoburg Forest, 'Aftermath'
sources.excerpt: Tiberius waged three subsequent campaigns against the Germanic tribes, but he chose not to occupy their land east of the Rhine. Instead, he stationed at least eight legions along the frontier to safeguard the provinces of eastern Gaul against a Germanic invasion.

zh: 战后，提比略又对日耳曼部落发动三次战役，但选择不占领莱茵河以东的土地，而是在边境驻扎至少八个军团。
en: After the battle, Tiberius waged three more campaigns against the Germanic tribes, but chose not to occupy their land east of the Rhine and stationed at least eight legions on the frontier.

note.zh: 三次战役、八个军团照条目；不写“罗马从此一蹶不振”。
note.en: Three campaigns and eight legions follow the entry; Rome is not described as permanently broken.

statement.zh: 苏埃托尼乌斯记载，奥古斯都数月不理发须，并反复呼喊“瓦鲁斯，把军团还给我”。这条记载来自后世传记，不能当作现场记录。
statement.en: Suetonius writes that Augustus went months without cutting his hair or beard and repeatedly cried, “Varus, give me back my legions.” This story comes from a later biography and is not a contemporaneous record.

sources.locator: Britannica, Battle of the Teutoburg Forest, 'Aftermath', Suetonius
sources.excerpt: The historian Suetonius writes that Augustus went months without cutting his beard or hair—a sign of mourning in Roman religious tradition—and often wailed, “Quinctilius Varus, give me back my legions!”

zh: 苏埃托尼乌斯记载，奥古斯都数月不理发须，并反复呼喊“瓦鲁斯，把军团还给我”。
这条记载来自后世传记，不能当作现场记录。
en: Suetonius writes that Augustus went months without cutting his hair or beard and repeatedly cried, “Varus, give me back my legions.”
This story comes from a later biography and is not a contemporaneous record.

note.zh: 轶事标明来源与体裁，不当作现场记录。
note.en: The anecdote is attributed and genre-flagged, not treated as a contemporaneous record.

statement.zh: 条顿堡没有让罗马永久放弃日耳曼，但它确实阻止了罗马把莱茵河以东变成行省；此后的边界以莱茵河—多瑙河一线为主。
statement.en: Teutoburg did not make Rome abandon Germania forever, but it did stop Rome from turning the land east of the Rhine into a province; the frontier thereafter ran mainly along the Rhine and Danube.

zh: 条顿堡没有让罗马永久放弃日耳曼，但它确实阻止了罗马把莱茵河以东变成行省；此后的边界以莱茵河—多瑙河一线为主。
en: Teutoburg did not make Rome abandon Germania forever, but it did stop Rome from turning the land east of the Rhine into a province; the frontier thereafter ran mainly along the Rhine and Danube.

note.zh: 作者判断：把“停止设省”与“永久放弃”区分开。
note.en: Author judgment: distinguishes 'stopped making a province' from 'abandoned forever'.

title.en: Completion of the Roman Road System

summary.en: The Roman Empire continuously improved its road network, with total length exceeding 80,000 kilometers by the early 1st century AD. Each road had standard specifications, with milestones marking distances and waystations providing horse changes and lodging, greatly facilitating trade and military mobilization.

statement.zh: 罗马帝国持续完善道路网络，公元1世纪初总长超8万公里。
statement.en: The Roman Empire continuously improved its road network, with total length exceeding 80,000 kilometers by the early 1st century AD.

zh: 罗马帝国持续完善道路网络，公元1世纪初总长超8万公里。
en: The Roman Empire continuously improved its road network, with total length exceeding 80,000 kilometers by the early 1st century AD.

note.zh: 数字表述统一；事实待来源核验

statement.zh: 每条道路有标准规格，路边设里程碑标明距离，沿线有驿站提供换马和住宿，极大促进贸易和军事调动。
statement.en: Each road had standard specifications, with milestones marking distances and waystations providing horse changes and lodging, greatly facilitating trade and military mobilization.

en: Each road had standard specifications, with milestones marking distances and waystations providing horse changes and lodging, greatly facilitating trade and military mobilization.

title.en: Continued Academic Prosperity in Alexandria, Egypt

summary.en: Alexandria, under Roman rule, remained a Mediterranean center of learning. Although the Library of Alexandria had been damaged, it was still the largest collection of books. The Mouseion (temple of the Muses) gathered scholars from around the world, advancing knowledge in astronomy, mathematics, medicine, geography, and philosophy.

statement.zh: 罗马统治下的亚历山大城仍是地中海学术中心。亚历山大图书馆虽受损但仍是最大藏书机构，缪斯学院聚集各地学者，在天文学、数学、医学、地理学和哲学等领域推进知识前沿。
statement.en: Alexandria, under Roman rule, remained a Mediterranean center of learning.

zh: 罗马统治下的亚历山大城仍是地中海学术中心。亚历山大图书馆虽受损但仍是最大藏书机构，缪斯学院聚集各地学者，在天文学、数学、医学、地理学和哲学等领域推进知识前沿。
罗马统治下的亚历山大城仍是地中海学术中心。

title.en: Wang Mang Changed the Title of the Xiongnu Chanyu

summary.en: To display the Xin dynasty's authority and belittle the Xiongnu, Wang Mang changed the Xiongnu Chanyu's title to 'Jiangnu Fuyu' (Submissive Slave Servant). This insulting title change infuriated the Xiongnu Chanyu, leading to a sharp deterioration in Han-Xiongnu relations and renewed warfare along the frontier.

statement.zh:
王莽为彰显新朝权威、贬低匈奴，将匈奴单于称号改为“降奴服于”。这一侮辱性改号激怒匈奴单于，导致汉匈关系急剧恶化，边疆战事再起。名号之争触及草原政权的尊严与互市利益，单于以侵边回应；外交失礼迅速转为军事对抗。新朝的边疆政策由此受挫。

title.en: Wang Mang's Second Currency Reform

summary.en: Wang Mang launched a second currency reform, abolishing the inscribed knife and 'wrong' knife coins, and minting small coins and large fifty coins for concurrent use. The overvaluation of the large coins led to widespread counterfeiting, creating even more economic chaos.

statement.zh:
王莽推出第二次币制改革，废止契刀、错刀，改铸小钱与大钱五十并行。币值虚高导致民间盗铸盛行，经济秩序更加混乱。改革频繁更换币种与面值，使交易缺乏稳定尺度；大钱名义价值远高于金属含量，诱使私铸。货币失信进一步动摇新朝的经济基础。

title.en: Abolished Military Agriculture in Wuyuan and Other Commanderies

summary.en: Wang Mang ordered the abolition of military agricultural colonies in Wuyuan Commandery and other northern frontier regions. These colonies had been important for supplying food to border defense forces, and their abolition weakened the ability of the border areas to feed themselves.

statement.zh: 王莽下令撤销五原郡等北方边境的军事屯田。屯田原是供应边防军粮的重要制度，撤销后削弱了边境粮食自给能力。屯田以戍卒与移民耕作为基础，兼有守边与积谷的双重作用；撤废之后，边军需依赖内郡转运，粮价与运输成本上升。这道诏令也反映新朝在财政与边防之间的取舍。

title.en: Arminius United the Germanic Tribes

summary.en: In AD 11, Arminius, chief of the Germanic Cherusci tribe, after his great victory over the Roman legions at Teutoburg Forest, continued to unify neighboring Germanic tribes. He formed an anti-Roman alliance including the Bructeri and Marsi. This move fundamentally checked the Roman Empire's expansion into Germania.

statement.zh: 公元11年，日耳曼切鲁西部落首领阿尔米尼乌斯在条顿堡森林大胜罗马军团后继续统一周边日耳曼部落。他联合布鲁克泰里、马西人等部落形成了反罗马联盟。此举使罗马帝国在日耳曼尼亚的扩张受到根本性遏制。

title.en: Parthian Civil War: Rise of Artabanus II

summary.en: Power struggles were intense within the Parthian Empire. Artabanus II, the governor of Media, defeated his rivals and rose to prominence, later becoming king of Parthia. He successfully challenged Roman hegemony in the East.

statement.zh: 帕提亚帝国内部权力斗争激烈，米底总督阿尔达班二世击败其他竞争者崛起，后成为帕提亚国王，成功挑战罗马在东方霸权。他从帝国东北部起兵，依靠地方贵族与骑兵的支持入主中枢；王位更替频繁削弱了中央，阿尔达班以军事胜利与和约维持边疆。东方局势由此再度紧张。
statement.en: The internal power struggle in the Parthian Empire was fierce.

statement.zh: 王莽称帝后改变了对西域各国的政策，降低其王号为"侯"，引起西域诸国强烈不满。焉耆率先反叛新朝攻杀西域都护但钦。随后各国纷纷归附匈奴。王莽派兵征讨失利，丝绸之路中断。这是王莽外交政策的重大失败。
statement.en:
After Wang Mang declared himself emperor, he changed his policy towards the various kingdoms of the Western Regions, demoting their kingly titles to 'Marquis'. This aroused strong discontent. Yānqí (Karashahr) was the first to rebel, killing the Xin dynasty's Protector General of the Western Regions, Dan Qin. Subsequently, various kingdoms submitted to the Xiongnu. Wang Mang sent an expedition to punish them but was defeated, and the Silk Road was interrupted. This was a major failure of Wang Mang's foreign policy.

title.en: Wang Mang Re-established Xihe Officials and Implemented the Five Equalisations and Six Controls

summary.en: Wang Mang implemented the 'Five Equalisations and Six Controls' system: the government controlled the management of salt, iron, liquor, coinage, credit, and famous mountains and marshes. This was the core of the state monopoly economic policy, further intensifying social contradictions.

statement.zh:
王莽推行五均六筦制度：官府控制盐、铁、酒、铸钱、赊贷和名山大泽经营，是国家垄断经济政策的核心，加剧了社会矛盾。垄断把财政汲取扩展到日常生计，价格与借贷由官府掌握；商人与百姓的负担加重。经济统制未能稳定新朝。

把「王莽重设羲和命士、推行五均六筦」放回公元14年的新朝，可以看到经济变化的一个具体切面。

title.en: Peasant Uprising in Wuyuan and Dai Commanderies

summary.en: A large-scale peasant uprising broke out in Wuyuan and Dai commanderies under Xin rule. Due to oppressive policies, heavy corvée labor, and consecutive years of drought, the people of the northern border areas could no longer bear the burden and rose in revolt.

statement.zh:
新朝统治下的五原郡和代郡爆发大规模农民起义。因苛政、繁重徭役和连年旱灾，北方边境百姓不堪重负，纷纷揭竿而起。边郡的屯戍与转输叠加天灾，生计断绝后聚众攻掠；地方秩序松动，镇压与招抚交替。起义显示新朝基层控制的脆弱。

把「五原、代郡百姓起义」放回公元15年的新朝，可以看到军事变化的一个具体切面。

title.en: Romanization of Southern Britain

summary.en: The Roman Empire promoted Romanization in southern Britain. Law, currency, language, and construction techniques were gradually introduced, and local Celtic aristocrats began to adopt the Roman way of life.

statement.zh: 罗马帝国在不列颠南部推进罗马化，法律、货币、语言和建筑技术逐步推广，当地凯尔特贵族开始接受罗马生活方式。殖民城市、道路与浴场把罗马制度植入乡野，贵族通过担任市政官职获得公民身份；拉丁语在城市与官方场合通行，本地传统则在乡村延续。文化融合是渐进的。

title.en: Wang Mang Changed Official Titles Again

summary.en: Wang Mang once again massively changed the names of central and local official positions, changing many to ancient titles from the 'Rites of Zhou', such as changing 'Da Sinong' (Minister of Finance) to 'Xihe' and 'Taishou' (Commandery Governor) to 'Dayin', causing administrative confusion.

statement.zh:
王莽再次大规模更改中央和地方官职名称，将许多官职改为《周礼》古称，如大司农改羲和、太守改大尹，造成行政混乱。更名以复古为号召，试图借经典重塑官僚秩序；新旧名称并行使文书与考核失序。行政效率因形式改革而下降。

把「王莽更定官职名称」放回公元15年的新朝，可以看到政治变化的一个具体切面。

title.en: Kujula Kadphises United the Five Yuezhi Tribes

summary.en: Around AD 15, Kujula Kadphises, chief of the Kushan tribe (one of the five Yuezhi Xihou), unified the other four tribes through war and diplomacy. Kujula Kadphises established his capital at Bactra (modern Balkh, Afghanistan), proclaimed himself 'King of Kings', and founded the Kushan Empire. He issued gold coins in the Roman style and controlled Silk Road trade.

title.en: Roman-Dacian War

title.en: Wang Mang's Campaign Against the Southwestern Yi Failed

summary.en: Wang Mang dispatched General Lian Dan to lead an expedition against the Jutian Kingdom of the Southwestern Yi. Due to the difficult terrain, long supply lines, and stubborn resistance of the tribal peoples, the Xin forces suffered heavy losses, deepening the fiscal crisis.

statement.zh: 王莽派遣将军廉丹率军征讨西南夷句町国。因地理复杂、补给线长及部族顽强抵抗，新军遭受重创，加深财政危机。西南山地交通困难，军粮需分段转运，疫病与瘴气又削弱兵员；句町依托地形与部族联盟抵抗，使远征难以速决。失败与北方屯田的废罢叠加，暴露新朝边防的脆弱。

title.en: Germanicus Won Another Great Victory

summary.en: The Roman general Germanicus defeated the Germanic allied forces led by Arminius at the Battle of Idistaviso in Germania, achieving a significant victory.

statement.zh:
罗马将领日耳曼尼库斯在日耳曼尼亚的伊迪斯塔维索平原战役中击败阿尔米尼乌斯率领的日耳曼联军，取得重要胜利。此役以步兵阵线与骑兵配合击破森林中的伏击，罗马得以收复失地与军旗；胜利未能转化为长期占领。边境政策仍在进攻与撤退之间摇摆。

把「日耳曼尼库斯再获大胜」放回公元16年的罗马帝国，可以看到军事变化的一个具体切面。
statement.en: The Roman general Germanicus defeated the German army led by Arminius at the Battle of Edistaviso Plain in Germania and achieved an important victory.

title.en: Guo Tianyi of Linhuai Rebelled

summary.en: Guo Tianyi from Linhuai Commandery gathered followers and rebelled in the Kuaiji region. This was one of the earliest peasant uprisings during the Xin dynasty, using mountainous terrain as a base and repeatedly defeating government forces, opening the prelude to nationwide anti-Wang Mang revolts.

title.en: Wang Mang Sent People to Seek Immortals and Magical Arts

summary.en: Imitating Emperor Wu of Han, Wang Mang sent numerous magicians across the country to search for immortals and the arts of longevity. He held sacrificial ceremonies for immortals in the palace, attempting to maintain his ruling confidence through mysticism.

title.en: Outbreak of the Lülin (Greenwood) Rebellion

summary.en: Due to consecutive years of famine in the Jingzhou region, starving peasants led by Wang Kuang and Wang Feng gathered to rebel, using Mount Lülin as their base. They were called the 'Lülin Army' and quickly grew to tens of thousands, becoming one of the main anti-Wang Mang forces.

statement.zh: 荆州地区连年饥荒，饥民在王匡、王凤领导下聚众起义，以绿林山为根据地，称“绿林军”，迅速发展到数万人规模，成为反莽主力之一。
statement.en:
Due to consecutive years of famine in the Jingzhou region, starving peasants led by Wang Kuang and Wang Feng gathered to rebel, using Mount Lülin as their base. They were called the 'Lülin Army' and quickly grew to 10,000, becoming one of the main anti-Wang Mang forces.

For Asia in 17 CE, “Outbreak of the Lülin (Greenwood) Rebellion” is a traceable node of Military change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Germanicus Recalled to Rome

summary.en: In AD 17, Roman Emperor Tiberius, fearing that Germanicus's successes in Germania might threaten his position, recalled him to Rome. After achieving major military victories (including capturing Arminius's stronghold), Germanicus was ordered to go east to handle affairs in Armenia. He died mysteriously in Antioch in AD 19.

title.en: Outbreak of the Red Eyebrow Rebellion

summary.en: Fan Chong from Langye Commandery gathered followers and rebelled in Ju County. To distinguish themselves from government troops, they dyed their eyebrows red and were therefore called the 'Red Eyebrow Army', rapidly developing into a huge armed force numbering hundreds of thousands.

title.en: Arminius Assassinated

summary.en: The Germanic hero Arminius was assassinated by his own family members due to internal power struggles. His death led to the disintegration of the Germanic tribal alliance, reducing pressure on the Roman frontier.

statement.zh:
日耳曼英雄阿尔米尼乌斯因内部权力斗争被家族成员刺杀。他的死使日耳曼部落联盟解体，罗马在边境压力减轻。阿尔米尼乌斯曾联合诸部对抗罗马，战后声望日盛，也引起族内猜忌；刺杀之后，联盟失去核心，各部重新分散。罗马得以在莱茵河一线调整防务。

把「阿尔米尼乌斯遇刺身亡」放回公元18年的日耳曼尼亚，可以看到政治变化的一个具体切面。

title.en: Diao Zidu of Donghai Rebelled

summary.en: Diao Zidu from Donghai Commandery gathered followers and rebelled, leading starving peasants to attack government offices and open granaries for relief. This was an important component of the anti-Wang Mang uprising in the east, echoing the Lülin and Red Eyebrow forces.

statement.zh:
东海郡人刁子都聚众起义，领导饥民攻打官府、开仓放粮，是东方反莽起义的重要组成部分，与绿林、赤眉遥相呼应。起义以饥荒与赋役为背景，流民结队攻仓夺粮；东方与荆州、青徐的起事形成呼应。新朝的地方控制迅速瓦解。

title.en: Germanicus Sent East

summary.en: Emperor Tiberius sent Germanicus to the East to handle affairs in Armenia and Syria. Ostensibly an important assignment, it was actually a move to remove him from the Germanic legions and diminish his power.

statement.zh:
提比略皇帝将日耳曼尼库斯派往东方处理亚美尼亚和叙利亚事务，表面委以重任，实为调离日耳曼军团以削弱其势力。东方行省与帕提亚接壤，外交与军权集中，任命既可安边也可监控；日耳曼尼库斯在任上去世，死因引发猜疑。皇室内部的猜忌影响了帝国政治。

title.en: Intensifying Social Contradictions in the Province of Judea

summary.en: Social contradictions were sharp in the Roman province of Judea: repressive Roman policies, heavy taxation, and provocations against Jewish customs aroused strong discontent, while internal Jewish factions (Sadducees, Pharisees, Zealots) fought among themselves, sowing the seeds for the future Jewish War.

statement.zh: 罗马犹太行省社会矛盾尖锐：罗马高压政策、沉重赋税和对犹太习俗的冒犯激起强烈不满，犹太内部撒都该派、法利赛派、奋锐党等相互争斗，为日后犹太战争埋下根源。

title.en: Wang Mang Cast the 'Wei Dou' as a Symbol of Power

summary.en: Wang Mang ordered the casting of a 'Wei Dou' (Power Dipper) from bronze, imitating the shape of the Northern Dipper constellation, believing it was the 'celestial pivot' and that the Dipper symbolized his authority coming from Heaven's mandate. Each time he traveled, he had the Wei Dou carried before him to display his sanctity.

title.en: Widespread Uprisings in Hebei and Shandong

summary.en: A wave of large-scale peasant uprisings broke out in Hebei and Shandong. The middle and lower reaches of the Yellow River suffered from floods, droughts, and oppressive government. Rebel groups ranged from tens of thousands to a few thousand, rising one after another.

statement.zh:
新莽末年，河北和山东地区爆发大规模农民起义浪潮。黄河中下游饱受水旱灾害和苛政之苦，各地义军多者数万、少者数千，此起彼伏。起义以流民与地方豪杰为骨干，缺乏统一号令；官军疲于奔命，地方秩序崩解。新朝的统治基础迅速瓦解。

title.en: Wang Mang Issued Strict Order: 'Those Who Dared Counterfeit Coins Would Be Executed'

summary.en: Counterfeiting of coins became increasingly rampant among the people. Wang Mang issued a strict order: those who dared to counterfeit coins would be executed. Despite the harsh penalty, counterfeiting continued unabated, only exacerbating social conflicts.

statement.zh:
民间盗铸钱币之风愈演愈烈，王莽颁布严令：敢盗铸钱者处死。尽管刑罚残酷，盗铸活动依然屡禁不止，反而加剧社会矛盾。严刑源于币值虚高与私铸获利，官府以死刑与连坐威慑，却难以根除地下铸造；告发与株连又伤及无辜。货币危机转为治安与信任危机。

把「王莽颁布‘敢盗铸钱者处死’严令」放回公元21年的新朝，可以看到经济变化的一个具体切面。
statement.en: Counterfeiting of coins became increasingly rampant among the people.

title.en: Anti-Wang Mang Uprisings Swept the Country

summary.en: Anti-Wang Mang uprisings spread from localized areas across the nation, from Hebei in the north to Jingzhou in the south, from Shandong in the east to Guanzhong in the west. Rebel groups rose everywhere, and the Xin dynasty's ruling system was on the verge of collapse.

statement.zh:
反莽起义从局部蔓延全国，北起河北、南至荆州，东起山东、西至关中，各地义军此起彼伏，新朝统治体系濒临崩溃。起义以饥荒、徭役与改制的失败为背景，绿林、赤眉等队伍在流民中壮大；地方官府失去控制，豪强结寨自保。新朝的合法性在军事失败中迅速流失。

title.en: Roman Emperor Tiberius Retired to Capri

summary.en: In AD 21, Roman Emperor Tiberius left Rome and went into seclusion on the island of Capri in the Bay of Naples. He built twelve luxurious villas (named after Greek gods) on the island, controlling the empire's administration through letters and coded messages. Tiberius's seclusion allowed Sejanus, the Praetorian Prefect, to gain increasing power in Rome.

title.en: Lülin Army Decisively Defeated Xin Forces at the Bishui River

summary.en: In the third year of Wang Mang's Dihuang era (AD 22), the Lülin Army defeated the Xin Mang government forces at the Bishui River (modern Biyang, Henan). statement.zh: 王莽地皇三年（公元22年），绿林军在沘水（今河南泌阳）大败新莽官军。绿林军本是荆州饥民起义军，分下江和新市两股。两军在沘水击败了莽军大将严尤和陈茂的部队，斩杀数千人。此战标志着绿林军从流动作战转向正面与官军对抗，随后绿林军拥立刘玄为更始帝，成为推翻新朝的主要力量之一。
statement.en:
In the third year of Wang Mang's Dihuang era (AD 22), the Lülin Army defeated the Xin Mang government forces at the Bishui River (modern Biyang, Henan). The Lülin Army originated from starving peasants in Jingzhou, splitting into Xiàjiang (Lower River) and Xinshi (New Market) groups. The two groups defeated the Xin commanders Yan You and Chen Mao's forces at the Bishui, killing several 1000 soldiers. This battle marked the Lülin Army's transition from guerrilla warfare to open confrontation with government forces. Subsequently, the Lülin Army supported Liu Xuan as Emperor Gengshi, becoming a major force in overthrowing the Xin dynasty.

For Asia in 22 CE, “Lülin Army Decisively Defeated Xin Forces at the Bishui River” is a traceable node of Military change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Liu Xiu and Liu Yan Raised Troops at Chongling

summary.en: A ninth-generation descendant of Emperor Gaozu of Han, Liu Xiu, together with his elder brother Liu Yan, gathered over 8,000 Han clan members and followers at Chongling to rise in rebellion against Wang Mang. This force later became the backbone for overthrowing the Xin dynasty and restoring the Han dynasty.

statement.zh: 新莽末年，汉高祖九世孙刘秀与兄长刘縯在舂陵召集汉宗族子弟八千余人起兵反莽，这支队伍后来成为推翻新朝和重建汉朝的骨干力量。起兵以宗族、宾客与地方豪杰为基干，初起时兵少粮缺，屡遭挫败；兄弟二人分工统军，逐步吸纳各路义军。复兴汉室的旗帜由此立起。
statement.en: In the last years of Wang Mang's Xin, Liu Xiu, a ninth-generation descendant of Emperor Gaozu, and his elder brother Liu Yan gathered over eight thousand Han clansmen and followers at Chongling to rise against Wang Mang; the force later became the backbone that overthrew Xin and restored Han.

title.en: Great Famine in Guanzhong, Cannibalism Reported

summary.en: A severe famine struck the Guanzhong region, capital of the Xin dynasty. Grain prices skyrocketed, corpses littered the roads, and there were even reports of cannibalism. The Wang Mang government was unable to provide relief, and masses of starving people flooded into Chang'an seeking survival.

statement.zh: 新朝首都关中地区发生严重饥荒，粮价飞涨、饿殍载道，甚至出现人吃人惨况；王莽政府无力赈灾，大量饥民涌入长安求生。粮价飞涨、饿殍与食人记载层层递进，说明饥荒已经越过普通歉收，进入社会秩序崩解的阶段；政府无力赈灾，则使灾民只能向首都集中，进一步加重了当地的供给压力。
statement.en: A severe famine struck Guanzhong, capital region of the Xin dynasty.

title.en: Wang Mang Was Beheaded, Xin Dynasty Fell

summary.en: In October, the Lülin Army entered Chang'an. Wang Mang fled in the chaos to the Terrace at Dutai (Jiantai), where he was killed by a merchant named Du Wu. His body was dismembered, and his head was sent around the country for public display. The Xin dynasty had lasted only fifteen years.

statement.zh:
十月，绿林军攻入长安，王莽在混乱中逃至渐台被商人杜吴杀死。尸体被肢解，首级传送各地示众，新朝共历15年而亡。都城失守使符命与改制的话语彻底破产，吏民与商贩在乱中自保；首级传递成为胜利者的宣示，改制多依古制，钱法混乱，民间私铸盛行。

把「王莽被斩首，新朝灭亡」放回公元23年的新朝，可以看到政治变化的一个具体切面。
statement.en:
In October, the Lülin Army entered Chang'an. Wang Mang fled in the chaos to the Terrace at Dutai (Jiantai), where he was killed by a merchant named Du Wu. His body was dismembered, and his head was sent around the country for public display. The Xin dynasty had lasted only 15 years. The loss of the capital discredited the rhetoric of portents and reform, officials and traders looked to their own safety, and the travelling head proclaimed the victors; the reforms had followed ancient models, coinage fell into disorder and private minting flourished.

It sits within the timeline's chronological coverage of Xin Dynasty and politics history.

title.en: Tiberius and Sejanus Co-ruled

summary.en: In AD 23, Tiberius granted Sejanus the Praetorian Prefect equal consular power ('imperium proconsulare'), making them formally co-rulers. Sejanus became the second most powerful person in the empire, second only to Tiberius. However, his ambitions aroused Tiberius's suspicions, ultimately leading to his downfall.

title.en: Lülin Army Supported Liu Xuan as Emperor (Emperor Gengshi)

summary.en: The Lülin Army supported Liu Xuan as emperor at Wancheng, changing the era name to Gengshi. Liu Xuan was a cousin of Liu Xiu. After proclaiming himself emperor, Gengshi appointed Liu Xiu as General of the Left Flank. The establishment of the Gengshi regime provided a unified banner for the anti-Wang Mang forces.

statement.zh: 绿林军在宛城拥立刘玄为帝，改元更始。刘玄是刘秀族兄，立帝后封刘秀为偏将军，更始政权建立使反莽势力有了统一旗帜。更始政权以恢复汉室为号召，整合各路义军，却因内部猜忌与用人失当而难以稳固；刘秀被派往河北，反而获得独立发展的机会。反莽的旗帜下已埋下分裂。
statement.en: The Lülin army enthroned Liu Xuan at Wancheng and changed the era name to Gengshi.

title.en: Emperor Gengshi Moved the Capital to Chang'an

summary.en: Emperor Gengshi moved the capital from Luoyang to Chang'an. As the former capital of the Western Han, Chang'an held political symbolic significance. However, after entering Chang'an, the Gengshi army's discipline broke down, and they looted the city, rapidly losing popular support.

title.en: Sejanus Persecuted Opposition

summary.en: In AD 24, Sejanus systematically eliminated political opponents in Rome. Taking advantage of Tiberius's trust, he prosecuted numerous noble senators under the charge of 'maiestas' (treason). Many senators were executed or exiled, and their property confiscated. Sejanus also attempted to marry Tiberius's niece Livilla to become a member of the imperial family.

title.en: Liu Xiu Established the Eastern Han (Guangwu Restoration)

summary.en: In June, Liu Xiu ascended the throne as emperor at the Qianqiu Pavilion in Hao City, changing the era name to Jianwu. The national title remained 'Han', and he established the capital at Luoyang (called Eastern Han because it was east of Chang'an). Liu Xiu was known as Emperor Guangwu of Han, and he initiated the 'Guangwu Restoration'.

statement.zh: 六月，刘秀在鄗城千秋亭登基称帝，改元建武，国号仍为“汉”，定都洛阳（因在长安之东，史称东汉）。刘秀即汉光武帝，开创“光武中兴”局面。
statement.en:
In June, Liu Xiu ascended the throne as emperor at the Qianqiu Pavilion in Hao City, changing the era name to Jianwu. The national title remained 'Han', and he established the capital at Luoyang (called Eastern Han because it was east of Chang'an). Liu Xiu was known as Emperor Guangwu of Han, and he initiated the 'Guangwu Restoration'.

For Asia in 25 CE, “Liu Xiu Established the Eastern Han (Guangwu Restoration)” is a traceable node of Politics change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Red Eyebrow Army Captured Chang'an, Gengshi Regime Fell

summary.en: In AD 25, the Red Eyebrow Army entered Chang'an. Emperor Gengshi, Liu Xuan, surrendered and was subsequently killed, marking the end of the Gengshi regime. In the same year, Liu Xiu declared himself emperor, establishing the Eastern H

statement.zh: 公元25年，赤眉军攻入长安，更始帝刘玄投降后被杀，更始政权覆灭。赤眉军在樊崇率领下立刘盆子为帝，但在长安放纵劫掠，很快失去民心。同年刘秀称帝建立东汉。
statement.en:
In AD 25, the Red Eyebrow Army entered Chang'an. Emperor Gengshi, Liu Xuan, surrendered and was subsequently killed, marking the end of the Gengshi regime. Led by Fan Chong, the Red Eyebrow Army supported Liu Penzi as emperor, but they looted and plundered in Chang'an, quickly losing popular support. In the same year, Liu Xiu declared himself emperor, establishing the Eastern Han dynasty.

For Asia in 25 CE, “Red Eyebrow Army Captured Chang'an, Gengshi Regime Fell” is a traceable node of Military change whose significance is best read through later events.

zh: 公元25年，赤眉军攻入长安，更始帝刘玄投降后被杀，更始政权覆灭。赤眉军在樊崇率领下立刘盆子为帝，但在长安放纵劫掠，很快失去民心。同年刘秀称帝建立东汉。
公元25年，赤眉军攻入长安，更始帝刘玄投降后被杀，更始政权覆灭。
en: In AD 25, the Red Eyebrow Army entered Chang'an. Emperor Gengshi, Liu Xuan, surrendered and was subsequently killed, marking the end of the Gengshi regime. Led by Fan Chong, the Red Eyebrow Army supported Liu Penzi as emperor, but they looted and plundered in Chang'an, quickly losing popular support. In the same year, Liu Xiu declared himself emperor, establishing the Eastern Han dynasty.

title.en: Caligula Lived with Tiberius on Capri

title.en: Red Eyebrow Army Pillaged Chang'an and Moved West

summary.en: With grain supplies exhausted in Guanzhong, the Red Eyebrow Army could not maintain their position and decided to withdraw westward. Before leaving, they pillaged Chang'an extensively, burning down the palaces and treasures accumulated by the Western Han over two centuries.

statement.zh:
关中粮草匮乏，赤眉军无法立足，决定向西撤离。撤离前在长安大肆焚掠，将西汉两百年积蓄的宫殿和珍宝付之一炬。流民武装缺乏稳定的补给与行政能力，占城而无法治理，只能以掠夺维持；西撤既是为就食，也标志其由盛转衰。长安的破坏使关中元气大伤。

title.en: Peng Chong of Yuyang Rebelled

summary.en: Peng Chong, Grand Administrator of Yuyang Commandery and a subordinate of Liu Xiu, rebelled due to dissatisfaction with Liu Xiu's suspicions. Peng Chong had been an important supporter of Liu Xiu in Hebei. His rebellion put Liu Xiu in a difficult position, having to fight on two fronts.

title.en: Emperor Guangwu Enfeoffed Founding Contributors

summary.en: Emperor Guangwu of Han enfeoffed his founding contributors as marquises. The most meritorious, including Deng Yu (Marquis of Liang), Wu Han (Marquis of Guangping), and Jia Fu (Marquis of Jiaodong), totaling over three hundred individuals. He provided generous treatment to these contributors but granted them no real power, preventing the rise of powerful ministers.

title.en: Sejanus Fell and Was Killed

summary.en: Sejanus, the Roman Praetorian Prefect, was suddenly arrested and executed on Tiberius's orders. Tiberius's order was delivered by letter. Sejanus was read his list of crimes and executed on the spot in the Senate, and his followers were also purged.

title.en: Jesus Began His Ministry

summary.en: Jesus of Nazareth began his public ministry in the region of Galilee, preaching the gospel of the kingdom of God, teaching repentance and love for others, and performing healings and miracles. His ministry attracted many followers but also aroused the suspicion of Jewish religious leaders.

title.en: Tiberius Continued the Reign of Terror

summary.en: In AD 28, Roman Emperor Tiberius continued to remotely control Rome's reign of terror from Capri. Numerous treason trials continued, and many senators were executed or forced to commit suicide. Informers were rewarded, and all of Roman society was enveloped in suspicion and fear. The power of Praetorian Prefect Sejanus continued to expand.

title.en: Emperor Guangwu Implemented Streamlining and Cost-Cutting

summary.en: Liu Xiu issued an edict to consolidate commanderies and counties, reducing the number of officials. Over 400 counties were merged, a large number of local officials were dismissed, and central government institutions were streamlined, reducing government spending to one-tenth of that in the late Western Han.

statement.zh:
刘秀下诏裁并郡县，精简官吏。合并四百余县，裁减大批地方官吏，同时压缩中央机构，将政府开支降至西汉末年的十分之一。诏令把重叠的行政层级合并，裁汰冗员、归并职能；地方治理的负担因此减轻。节俭政治成为新朝的气象。

把「刘秀推行精兵简政」放回公元28年的东汉，可以看到政治变化的一个具体切面。

title.en: Re-established the Imperial Academy and Revived Confucianism

summary.en: Liu Xiu ordered the reconstruction of the Imperial Academy in Luoyang, restoring the Confucian classics that had been damaged during the wars. The rebuilt academy gathered scholars from across the nation, the Erudites of the Five Classics resumed their teachings, and Confucianism was re-established as the official state ideology.

刘秀下令在洛阳重建太学，修复遭战乱破坏的儒家经典。重建后的太学汇集全国学者，五经博士恢复讲学，儒学重新确立官方意识形态地位。太学以经师讲学与博士制度培养官僚，修复经典把战乱中断的学术传统接续；儒学与选官结合。东汉的文教秩序由此重建。

把「设立太学，重振儒学」放回公元29年的东汉，可以看到文化变化的一个具体切面。
statement.en: Liu Xiu ordered the reconstruction of the Imperial Academy in Luoyang, restoring the Confucian classics that had been damaged during the wars.

title.en: Emperor Guangwu Reduced Land Tax to One-Thirtieth

statement.zh: 东汉建武五年（公元29年），光武帝刘秀下诏将田赋从西汉末年的十税一减轻为三十税一，与汉文帝时期的低税率一致。
statement.en: In the fifth year of the Jianwu era of Eastern Han (AD 29), Emperor Guangwu issued an edict reducing the land tax from one-tenth of the harvest (the rate in the late Western Han) to one-thirtieth, matching the low tax rate of Emperor Wen of Han's reign.

en: In the fifth year of the Jianwu era of Eastern Han (AD 29), Emperor Guangwu issued an edict reducing the land tax from one-tenth of the harvest (the rate in the late Western Han) to one-thirtieth, matching the low tax rate of Emperor Wen of Han's reign.

title.en: John the Baptist Preached

summary.en: John the Baptist preached in the region of the Jordan River, calling on people to repent and be baptized in preparation for the coming Messiah. John wore clothing made of camel's hair and ate locusts and wild honey. He was later imprisoned and beheaded for rebuking Herod Antipas for marrying his brother's wife.

statement.zh:
施洗约翰在约旦河一带传道，呼吁人们悔改受洗以迎接弥赛亚。约翰以骆驼毛为衣、蝗虫野蜜为食，后因指责希律·安提帕娶弟媳而被囚禁斩首。苦修与末世期待塑造其形象，洗礼成为悔改与净化的仪式；对权贵的批评招致杀身之祸。早期基督教运动由此获得先驱叙事。

title.en: Implementation of the Land Survey Decree Began

summary.en: Liu Xiu issued an edict implementing the Land Survey Decree (Dutian Ling) nationwide, ordering each commandery and county to survey and verify land holdings and household numbers. The aim was to fairly distribute the tax burden and increase government revenue. However, it infringed on the interests of local powerful families, leading to strong resistance.

statement.zh:
刘秀下诏在全国推行度田令，命令各州郡清查核实土地数量和户口情况，旨在公平赋税负担、增加财政收入。但触犯地方豪强利益，遭到强烈抵制。清查以自报与核实相结合，官吏却与豪强通同隐匿；朝廷以严刑督责，反激起地方骚动。度田在执行中折中收场。

把「度田令开始推行」放回公元30年的东汉，可以看到经济变化的一个具体切面。

title.en: Tiberius Summoned Caligula

summary.en: Emperor Tiberius, living in seclusion on Capri, summoned the young Caligula to his side to be personally trained. On the island, Caligula learned to hide his true feelings and feign obedience.

statement.zh:
隐居卡普里岛的提比略皇帝将年轻的卡利古拉召到身边亲自培养。卡利古拉在岛上学会隐藏真实情感和伪装顺从。提比略以试探与观察考察继承人，卡利古拉则以恭顺姿态取得信任；这段经历塑造了他的行事方式。

把「提比略召卡利古拉到身边」放回公元30年的罗马帝国，可以看到政治变化的一个具体切面。

summary.en: Du Shi, Grand Administrator of Nanyang during the Eastern Han, summarized the experiences of the working people and invented the water-powered bellows (Shui Pai). title.en: Jesus Predicted the Destruction of Jerusalem

summary.en: According to the Bible, Jesus predicted on the Mount of Olives that the Temple in Jerusalem would be completely destroyed. This prophecy was fulfilled in AD 70 when Roman legions captured Jerusalem.

statement.zh:
据《圣经》记载，耶稣在橄榄山上预言耶路撒冷圣殿将被彻底摧毁。这一预言在公元70年罗马军团攻陷耶路撒冷时成为现实。预言把圣殿的命运与末世论相连，早期教会以此解释灾难；罗马镇压与犹太战争使圣殿真的被毁。文本与历史在后世被反复对照。

把「耶稣预言耶路撒冷毁灭」放回公元32年的犹太，可以看到宗教变化的一个具体切面。

title.en: Emperor Guangwu Personally Led Campaign Against Wei Xiao

summary.en: Liu Xiu personally led a major expedition against the separatist Wei Xiao in Longxi. Wei Xiao outwardly submitted to the Eastern Han but secretly colluded with Gongsun Shu. Liu Xiu decided to take advantage of Wei Xiao's unstable position to pacify Longxi once and for all.

statement.zh:
刘秀亲自率领大军征讨陇西割据势力隗嚣。隗嚣表面臣服东汉，实则暗中勾结公孙述，刘秀决定趁其立足未稳一举平定陇西。远征以粮道与山地攻坚为难点，汉军分路推进，招降与用兵并用；隗嚣据险坚守，战事迁延。西部的统一由此提上日程。

statement.zh: 东汉建武九年（公元33年），盘踞陇西（今甘肃东部）的割据势力首领隗嚣病逝。隗嚣原为更始帝的部下，后在刘秀与公孙述之间摇摆不定。隗嚣临死前将权力交给其子隗纯，隗纯继位后继续抵抗东汉的统一。光武帝刘秀趁隗嚣新丧、内部不稳之机，于33-34年发动大规模进攻，最终攻破隗纯据守的落门聚（今天水武山），隗纯投降，陇西平定。
statement.en:
In the ninth year of the Jianwu era of Eastern Han (AD 33), Wei Xiao, the warlord controlling Longxi (eastern Gansu), died of illness. Wei Xiao had originally been a subordinate of Emperor Gengshi, wavering between Liu Xiu and Gongsun Shu. Before his death, Wei Xiao passed his power to his son Wei Chun, who continued to resist Eastern Han unification. Emperor Guangwu took advantage of Wei Xiao's recent death and internal instability to launch a massive offensive between AD 33-34, ultimately capturing Luomenju (modern Wushan, Tianshui) where Wei Chun was holding out. Wei Chun surrendered, and Longxi was pacified.

For Asia in 33 CE, “Wei Xiao Died of Illness, Wei Chun Succeeded” is a traceable node of Politics change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Wu Han and Others Attacked Longxi

summary.en: Grand Marshal Wu Han led the main Eastern Han army in a fierce attack on Longxi, successively capturing the cities held by Wei Chun. The victory in the Longxi campaign brought the Hexi Corridor under Eastern Han control, opening the route to the Western Regions.

title.en: Jewish Governor Pilate Suppressed the Samaritans

summary.en: In AD 34, the Roman governor of Judea, Pontius Pilate, led forces to suppress a religious gathering of Samaritans on Mount Gerizim, where they claimed to have discovered sacred vessels of Moses. Pilate attacked, using the pretext that they were assembling to rebel, killing many. This led to Pilate being recalled to Rome for trial in AD 36.

title.en: Emperor Guangwu Issued Edicts to Free Slaves

summary.en: Emperor Guangwu issued multiple edicts to free slaves, stipulating that those who had been sold into slavery due to the wars could regain their civilian status. These measures helped alleviate social conflicts and restore productivity.

statement.zh:
光武帝刘秀多次下诏释放奴婢，规定因战乱被卖为奴者可以恢复平民身份。这些措施缓和社会矛盾，恢复生产力。诏令针对战乱中的债务奴役与掠卖，限定释放条件与年限，并要求地方执行；奴婢归籍后成为编户，承担赋役。政策有助于恢复户籍与农业生产。

把「刘秀下诏释放奴婢」放回公元34年的东汉，可以看到政治变化的一个具体切面。

statement.zh: 东汉建武十年（公元34年），光武帝刘秀派遣来歙、耿弇等将领率军围攻隗纯据守的最后据点落门（今天水武山县）。汉军使用攻城器械持续猛攻，隗纯部将王元等人投降。隗纯见大势已去被迫投降。陇西从此完全平定。至此刘秀已消灭了除公孙述之外的所有割据势力，东汉统一大业基本完成。
statement.en:
In the tenth year of the Jianwu era of Eastern Han (AD 34), Emperor Guangwu sent generals Lai Xi and Geng Yan to lead forces in besieging Wei Chun's last stronghold at Luomen (modern Wushan County, Tianshui). The Han forces used siege engines in continuous, fierce attacks. Wei Chun's subordinates, including Wang Yuan, surrendered. Seeing that the situation was hopeless, Wei Chun was forced to surrender. Longxi was thus completely pacified. By this time, Liu Xiu had eliminated all the separatist regimes except for Gongsun Shu, and the unification of the Eastern Han was essentially complete.

summary.en: In AD 38, Caligula's relationship with the Roman Senate deteriorated sharply. title.en: Caligula's Farce on the Rhine Frontier

summary.en: In AD 40, Caligula led a large army to the Rhine frontier, claiming to launch an expedition against the Germanic tribes. However, he merely had his troops 'fight a naval battle' on the coast (collecting seashells as 'spoils'), then returned to Rome. This ridiculous expedition exposed Caligula's mental instability and wasted a huge amount of military funds.

title.en: Emperor Guangwu Established Guo Shengtong as Empress

summary.en: During the establishment of the Eastern Han dynasty, to gain the support of powerful families in Hebei, Emperor Guangwu of Han married Guo Shengtong, the niece of Liu Yang, the Prince of Zhending, in the second year of the Jianwu era (AD 26), and later established her as Empress. statement.en: During the establishment of the Eastern Han dynasty, to gain the support of powerful families in Hebei, Emperor Guangwu of Han married Guo Shengtong, the niece of Liu Yang, the Prince of Zhending, in the second year of the Jianwu era (AD 26), and later established her as Empress.

en: During the establishment of the Eastern Han dynasty, to gain the support of powerful families in Hebei, Emperor Guangwu of Han married Guo Shengtong, the niece of Liu Yang, the Prince of Zhending, in the second year of the Jianwu era (AD 26), and later established her as Empress.

title.en: Claudius Conquered Britain

summary.en: Roman Emperor Claudius sent his general Aulus Plautius with a force of 40,000 men to invade Britain. They landed in Kent and defeated the local resistance. Claudius personally went to Britain to accept the surrender. By AD 47, the Romans controlled southern and central England and established the province of Britannia, which would last for nearly four hundred years.

statement.en:
Roman Emperor Claudius sent his general Aulus Plautius with a force of 40,000 men to invade Britain. They landed in Kent and defeated the local resistance. title.en: Wuling's Five Streams Barbarians Rebelled

summary.en: In the twenty-third year of the Jianwu era of Eastern Han (AD 47), the Five Streams Barbarians (Wuxi Man) tribe in Wuling Commandery (western Hunan) rebelled due to oppressive taxes and corvée labor imposed by local officials. Emperor Guangwu successively sent generals Liu Shang and Li Song to lead expeditions, but they were repeatedly defeated due to unfamiliarity with the mou

statement.zh: 东汉建武二十三年（公元47年），武陵郡（今湖南湘西）的五溪蛮部落因不堪地方官吏的苛捐杂税和徭役压迫起兵反叛。光武帝刘秀先后派遣刘尚、李嵩等将领率军征讨，但因不熟悉山地地形屡次战败。最后派遣伏波将军马援率四万大军征讨，马援采取缓进策略并在壶头山（今沅陵）扎营，但因军中瘟疫流行而受挫。马援病逝后东汉调整政策以招抚为主，至49年才基本平定。
statement.en:
In the twenty-third year of the Jianwu era of Eastern Han (AD 47), the Five Streams Barbarians (Wuxi Man) tribe in Wuling Commandery (western Hunan) rebelled due to oppressive taxes and corvée labor imposed by local officials. Emperor Guangwu successively sent generals Liu Shang and Li Song to lead expeditions, but they were repeatedly defeated due to unfamiliarity with the mountainous terrain. Finally, the Vanguard General Ma Yuan was dispatched with 40,000 troops. Ma Yuan adopted a cautious strategy and established his camp at Hutou Mountain (modern Yuanling), but his campaign was hampered by an epidemic in the army. After Ma Yuan died of illness, the Eastern Han adjusted its policy, focusing on pacification, and did not completely quell the rebellion until AD 49.

For Asia in 47 CE, “Wuling's Five Streams Barbarians Rebelled” is a traceable node of Military change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Ma Yuan Volunteered to Campaign Against the Five Streams Barbarians

summary.en: The 62-year-old veteran general Ma Yuan volunteered to lead the campaign against the Five Streams Barbarians, and Emperor Guangwu agreed. Ma Yuan led his army on the expedition, but due to tactical errors and unsuitable climate, the campaign bogged down.

statement.zh:
62岁的老将马援主动请缨征讨五溪蛮，刘秀同意。马援率军出征，但因战术失误和气候不适，战事陷入僵局。军队在湿热山地中疫病流行，补给困难，进退两难；马援病逝于军中，战事由他人接手。此次出征暴露出南方山地作战的困难。

把「马援请缨征五溪蛮」放回公元48年的东汉，可以看到军事变化的一个具体切面。
statement.en:
The 62-year-old veteran general Ma Yuan volunteered to lead the campaign against the Five Streams Barbarians, and Emperor Guangwu agreed. Ma Yuan led his army on the expedition, but due to tactical errors and unsuitable climate, the campaign bogged down. Epidemic spread in the hot, damp hills and supplies ran short, leaving the army stranded; Ma Yuan died in camp and others took over. The expedition exposed the difficulties of mountain warfare in the south.

It sits within the timeline's chronological coverage of Eastern Han and military history.

The event is treated as one node in a longer sequence of change across Asia.

The entry is kept as a concise record of that wider process rather than a standalone narrative.

title.en: Paul Wrote the First Epistle to the Corinthians

summary.en: During his third missionary journey, while at Ephesus, the Apostle Paul wrote the First Epistle to the Corinthians, addressing issues within the church. Its thirteenth chapter, the 'Hymn to Love', has become a classic of literature.

statement.zh:
使徒保罗在第三次传教旅行期间，于以弗所写下《哥林多前书》，讨论教会内部问题，其中第13章“爱的颂歌”成为文学经典。书信回应教会的纷争、礼仪与伦理问题，以劝勉与神学论证组织内容；爱的篇章把信仰表达为实践。文本兼具牧养与文学价值。

把「保罗撰写《哥林多前书》」放回公元53年的希腊，可以看到宗教变化的一个具体切面。
statement.en:
During his third missionary journey, while at Ephesus, the Apostle Paul wrote the First Epistle to the Corinthians, addressing issues within the church. Its 13th chapter, the 'Hymn to Love', has become a classic of literature. The letter answered disputes over conduct, ritual and ethics, organized as exhortation and theological argument; the chapter on love made faith a practice. The text has both pastoral and literary value.

It sits within the timeline's chronological coverage of Greece and religion history.

The event is treated as one node in a longer sequence of change across Europe.

The record is presented as part of the wider history of Greece rather than as an isolated incident.

It is one of the entries through which the timeline traces religion history in Greece across Europe.

title.en: The Guangwu Restoration Reached Its Peak

summary.en: In the mid-Jianwu era (around AD 55), in the later years of Emperor Guangwu's reign, the Eastern Han social economy reached its peak after thirty years of recovery. Guangwu's policies of land surveys (Dutian), tax reduction (one-thirtieth), freeing slaves, and building water conservancy led to significant growth in agricultural and handicraft production. The population graduall

statement.zh: 东汉建武中元年间（公元55年左右），光武帝刘秀在位后期，东汉社会经济经过三十年的恢复达到鼎盛。刘秀推行"度田"（核实土地）、减轻赋税（三十税一）、释放奴婢、兴修水利等一系列政策，使农业和手工业生产大幅增长。人口从西汉末年的萧条逐步回升，政治稳定、百姓乐业，史称"光武中兴"。刘秀以"柔道治国"的理念，奠定了东汉近两百年的基业。
statement.en:
In the mid-Jianwu era (around AD 55), in the later years of Emperor Guangwu's reign, the Eastern Han social economy reached its peak after thirty years of recovery. Guangwu's policies of land surveys (Dutian), tax reduction (one-thirtieth), freeing slaves, and building water conservancy led to significant growth in agricultural and handicraft production. The population gradually rebounded from the slump of the late Western Han. With political stability and people living in contentment, this period was known as the 'Guangwu Restoration'. Guangwu's philosophy of 'governing with soft power' (Roudao Zhiguo) laid the foundation for the Eastern Han dynasty, which lasted nearly two hundred years.

For Asia in 55 CE, “The Guangwu Restoration Reached Its Peak” is a traceable node of Politics change whose significance is best read through later events.

zh: 东汉建武中元年间（公元55年左右），光武帝刘秀在位后期，东汉社会经济经过三十年的恢复达到鼎盛。刘秀推行"度田"（核实土地）、减轻赋税（三十税一）、释放奴婢、兴修水利等一系列政策，使农业和手工业生产大幅增长。人口从西汉末年的萧条逐步回升，政治稳定、百姓乐业，史称"光武中兴"。刘秀以"柔道治国"的理念，奠定了东汉近两百年的基业。

en: In the mid-Jianwu era (around AD 55), in the later years of Emperor Guangwu's reign, the Eastern Han social economy reached its peak after thirty years of recovery. Guangwu's policies of land surveys (Dutian), tax reduction (one-thirtieth), freeing slaves, and building water conservancy led to significant growth in agricultural and handicraft production. The population gradually rebounded from the slump of the late Western Han. With political stability and people living in contentment, this period was known as the 'Guangwu Restoration'. Guangwu's philosophy of 'governing with soft power' (Roudao Zhiguo) laid the foundation for the Eastern Han dynasty, which lasted nearly two hundred years.

title.en: Construction of the Mingtang, Lingtai, and Biyong

summary.en: In the first year of the Jianwu Zhongyuan era of Eastern Han (AD 56), Emperor Guangwu ordered the construction of three major ritual buildings south of Luoyang: the Mingtang, the Lingtai, and the Biyong. The Mingtang was a venue for the emperor to hold court and perform sacrifices; the Lingtai was an astronomical observatory; and the Biyong was the location of the Imperial Acad

statement.zh: 东汉建武中元元年（公元56年），光武帝刘秀下令在洛阳城南兴建明堂、灵台和辟雍三大礼制建筑。明堂是帝王举行朝会和祭祀的场所；灵台是观星望气的天文台；辟雍是太学所在地，同时也是皇帝行养老礼之处。三大建筑体现了"天人合一"的儒家政治理念，是东汉初年礼仪制度建设的重要象征，为后世都城规划提供了范本。
statement.en:
In the first year of the Jianwu Zhongyuan era of Eastern Han (AD 56), Emperor Guangwu ordered the construction of three major ritual buildings south of Luoyang: the Mingtang, the Lingtai, and the Biyong. The Mingtang was a venue for the emperor to hold court and perform sacrifices; the Lingtai was an astronomical observatory; and the Biyong was the location of the Imperial Academy, where the emperor also performed ceremonies honoring the elderly. These three buildings embodied the Confucian political concept of 'unity of Heaven and humanity', representing an important symbol of ritual system construction in the early Eastern Han. They served as a model for subsequent capital city planning.

For Asia in 56 CE, “Construction of the Mingtang, Lingtai, and Biyong” is a traceable node of Culture change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Emperor Guangwu Performed the Fengshan Ceremony at Mount Tai

summary.en: In the first year of the Jianwu Zhongyuan era of Eastern Han (AD 56), Emperor Guangwu, following the examples of Qin Shi Huang and Emperor Wu of Han, journeyed to Mount Tai to perform the Fengshan ceremony. Fengshan was the highest ritual for ancient emperors to report their achievements to Heaven and Earth. Through this, Guangwu signified that the Eastern Han had received the

statement.zh: 东汉建武中元元年（公元56年），光武帝刘秀效仿秦始皇和汉武帝，前往泰山举行封禅大典。封禅是古代帝王向天地报告功德的最高礼仪，刘秀以此表明东汉上承天命、平定天下的大功。他率群臣登山祭天（封）并在梁父山祭地（禅），立碑刻石记述功业。此次封禅是东汉唯一一次封禅泰山，标志着光武帝对自己治世功绩的最终确认。
statement.en:
In the first year of the Jianwu Zhongyuan era of Eastern Han (AD 56), Emperor Guangwu, following the examples of Qin Shi Huang and Emperor Wu of Han, journeyed to Mount Tai to perform the Fengshan ceremony. Fengshan was the highest ritual for ancient emperors to report their achievements to Heaven and Earth. Through this, Guangwu signified that the Eastern Han had received the Mandate of Heaven and accomplished the great task of unifying the empire. He led his officials up the mountain to offer sacrifice to Heaven (Feng) and offered sacrifice to Earth at Mount Liangfu (Shan). A stele was erected to record his achievements. This was the only Fengshan ceremony performed during the Eastern Han, marking Emperor Guangwu's final affirmation of his own achievements.

For Asia in 56 CE, “Emperor Guangwu Performed the Fengshan Ceremony at Mount Tai” is a traceable node of Politics change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Emperor Guangwu Promulgated Prophetic Charts (Chenwei)

summary.en: In the first year of the Jianwu Zhongyuan era of Eastern Han (AD 56), Emperor Guangwu formally promulgated prophetic charts (Chenwei) to the nation, establishing them as official theology. Chenwei were a type of mystical prophecy popular since the late Western Han. Liu Xiu used prophecies such as the 'Red Talisman' (Chifu Fu) to legitimize his claim to the empire. He ordered th

statement.zh: 东汉建武中元元年（公元56年），光武帝刘秀正式向全国颁布图谶（谶纬图书），将其定为官方神学。谶纬是西汉末年以来流行的神秘预言学说，刘秀利用"赤伏符"等谶语证明其得天下的合法性。他命人整理校订谶纬文献八十一篇，使其成为国家意识形态的重要组成部分。谶纬在东汉政治和学术中占据重要地位，严重影响了东汉的思想文化和政治风气。
statement.en:
In the first year of the Jianwu Zhongyuan era of Eastern Han (AD 56), Emperor Guangwu formally promulgated prophetic charts (Chenwei) to the nation, establishing them as official theology. Chenwei were a type of mystical prophecy popular since the late Western Han. Liu Xiu used prophecies such as the 'Red Talisman' (Chifu Fu) to legitimize his claim to the empire. He ordered the compilation and editing of 81 volumes of Chenwei literature, making them an integral part of state ideology. Chenwei occupied an important position in Eastern Han politics and scholarship, significantly influencing the intellectual climate and political culture of the time.

For Asia in 56 CE, “Emperor Guangwu Promulgated Prophetic Charts (Chenwei)” is a traceable node of Culture change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: King of the Wo (Japan) Sent Envoys to Pay Tribute

summary.en: In the second year of the Jianwu Zhongyuan era of Eastern Han (AD 57), the king of the Wo state (a Yamato-era kingdom in northern Kyushu, Japan) sent envoys across the Korean Peninsula and the sea to Luoyang to pay tribute to the Eastern Han court. Emperor Guangwu bestowed upon them a gold seal inscribed with the characters 'Han Wei Wo Wang' (King of the Wo, a vassal of Han). T

statement.zh: 东汉建武中元二年（公元57年），倭奴国（日本九州北部的那马台国或早期倭国）国王遣使经朝鲜半岛渡海来到洛阳向东汉朝贡。光武帝刘秀赐予其"汉委奴国王"金印（1784年在福冈县志贺岛出土，是日本最早的国宝之一）。这是中日关系史上首次有明确文献记载的官方交往，标志着日本列岛早期政权开始与中华帝国建立朝贡关系。
statement.en:
In the second year of the Jianwu Zhongyuan era of Eastern Han (AD 57), the king of the Wo state (a Yamato-era kingdom in northern Kyushu, Japan) sent envoys across the Korean Peninsula and the sea to Luoyang to pay tribute to the Eastern Han court. Emperor Guangwu bestowed upon them a gold seal inscribed with the characters 'Han Wei Wo Wang' (King of the Wo, a vassal of Han). This seal, unearthed at Shikanoshima, Fukuoka Prefecture in 1784, is one of Japan's earliest national treasures. This event marks the first recorded official diplomatic contact in Sino-Japanese history, indicating that early polities in the Japanese archipelago began establishing tributary relations with the Chinese empire.

For Asia in 57 CE, “King of the Wo (Japan) Sent Envoys to Pay Tribute” is a traceable node of Diplomacy change whose significance is best read through later events.

In the second year of the Jianwu Zhongyuan era of Eastern Han (AD 57), the king of the Wo state (a Yamato-era kingdom in northern Kyushu, Japan) sent envoys across the Korean Peninsula and the sea to Luoyang to pay tribute to the Eastern Han court.

title.en: Paul Arrested and Sent to Rome

summary.en: In AD 57, the Apostle Paul was arrested in Jerusalem. Accused by Jewish religious leaders of violating the Law and defiling the Temple, he was tried before Roman Governor Felix and King Agrippa II. Paul used his Roman citizenship to appeal to Caesar. He was escorted to Rome around AD 60 and placed under house arrest pending the emperor's judgment.

title.en: Emperor Guangwu Died, Emperor Ming Ascended

summary.en: Emperor Guangwu of Han died of illness at the Southern Palace in Luoyang. His crown prince Liu Zhuang ascended the throne as Emperor Ming of Han. The 'Guangwu Restoration' initiated by Liu Xiu left a stable and prosperous empire for his son.

把「光武帝刘秀驾崩，汉明帝即位」放回公元57年的东汉，可以看到政治变化的一个具体切面。

title.en: Artabanus II of Parthia Died

statement.zh: 东汉永平元年（公元58年），汉明帝刘庄在即位后不久即着手清除前朝权臣势力。明帝将大司徒韩歆等先帝重臣调离核心岗位，任命自己信任的东宫旧臣掌握实权。同时严格控制外戚干政，其皇后马氏家族虽受尊崇但不得干预朝政。明帝以严明驭下的风格著称，在位期间朝廷纪律整肃，官员执行力大幅提升。
statement.en:
In the first year of the Yongping era of Eastern Han (AD 58), shortly after ascending the throne, Emperor Ming moved to eliminate powerful officials from the previous reign. He transferred high-ranking ministers like Han Xin, the Grand Minister of Education, from their core positions, appointing his own trusted former advisors to key posts. At the same time, he strictly controlled consort kin interference in politics. Although the family of his Empress Ma was respected, they could not interfere in court affairs. Emperor Ming was known for his stern and decisive leadership. During his reign, court discipline was rigorous, and official execution efficiency greatly increased.

For Asia in 58 CE, “Emperor Ming Eliminated Powerful Officials” is a traceable node of Politics change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Emperor Ming Performed the Ceremony of Respecting the Elderly at the Biyong

summary.en: In the second year of the Yongping era (AD 59), Emperor Ming personally went to the Biyong (Imperial Academy) in Luoyang to perform a grand ceremony honoring the elderly (Yanglao Li). This was an important Confucian ritual venerating the aged. Emperor Ming offered wine and food to the esteemed elders (over seventy years old) called the 'Three Elders' and 'Five Respected Elders'

statement.zh: 东汉明帝刘庄于永平二年（公元59年）亲临洛阳的辟雍（太学）举行隆重的养老礼。养老礼是儒家尊老敬老的重要礼仪，明帝向七十岁以上的三老五更（德高望重的老者）敬酒献食，以示尊崇。明帝还亲自讲解《尚书》等儒家经典，太学生和百官在旁听讲。此举大力推崇儒学孝道，使东汉社会形成了尊儒重教的氛围，推动了文化教育的发展。
statement.en:
In the second year of the Yongping era (AD 59), Emperor Ming personally went to the Biyong (Imperial Academy) in Luoyang to perform a grand ceremony honoring the elderly (Yanglao Li). This was an important Confucian ritual venerating the aged. Emperor Ming offered wine and food to the esteemed elders (over seventy years old) called the 'Three Elders' and 'Five Respected Elders', demonstrating respect for the elderly. The Emperor himself lectured on Confucian classics like the 'Book of Documents' before an audience of Imperial Academy students and officials. This ritual highly promoted Confucian filial piety, created an atmosphere of respect for Confucianism and education in Eastern Han society, and fostered the development of culture and education.

For Asia in 59 CE, “Emperor Ming Performed the Ceremony of Respecting the Elderly at the Biyong” is a traceable node of Culture change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Boudica's Revolt Suppressed

summary.en: In AD 61, the Roman governor of Britain, Gaius Suetonius Paulinus, suppressed the revolt of the Iceni people led by Boudica. Boudica had massacred about 70,000 Romans and pro-Roman Britons in various parts of Britain. Suetonius defeated the rebel army at the Battle of Watling Street, despite being outnumbered. Boudica took poison after her defeat.

title.en: Emperor Ming Performed the Plowing Ceremony

summary.en: In the fourth year of the Yongping era (AD 61), Emperor Ming personally performed the plowing ceremony (Jitian Li) in the eastern suburbs of Luoyang, holding a plow to till the ceremonial field to show the importance he placed on agriculture. statement.zh: 东汉明帝刘庄于永平四年（公元61年）亲自在洛阳东郊举行藉田礼，手持犁具耕种御田，以示对农业的重视。藉田礼是古代帝王劝农的重要仪式，天子亲耕籍田，收获用于宗庙祭祀。明帝在位期间多次举行藉田礼，还命令地方官员仿效，鼓励农民开垦荒地、兴修水利。明帝的这些举措促进了东汉农业经济的持续发展。
statement.en:
In the fourth year of the Yongping era (AD 61), Emperor Ming personally performed the plowing ceremony (Jitian Li) in the eastern suburbs of Luoyang, holding a plow to till the ceremonial field to show the importance he placed on agriculture. The plowing ceremony was an important ritual in which the emperor demonstrated his encouragement of agriculture. The harvest from the emperor's field was used for ancestral sacrifices. Emperor Ming performed the plowing ceremony multiple times during his reign and ordered local officials to follow suit, encouraging people to open wasteland and build water conservancy. These measures contributed to the continued development of the agricultural economy in the Eastern Han.

For Asia in 61 CE, “Emperor Ming Performed the Plowing Ceremony” is a traceable node of Economy change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Emperor Ming Implemented Strict Laws

summary.en: During his reign (AD 58-75), Emperor Ming departed from Emperor Guangwu's 'soft power' approach to governance, instead implementing strict laws and harsh punishments. He relied on harsh officials (Kuli) to crack down on law-breaking powerful families and repeatedly severely punished corrupt officials. He also dealt harshly with imperial clan members and nobles who broke the law

statement.zh: 东汉明帝刘庄在位期间（公元58-75年）一改光武帝的"柔道"治国路线，转而推行严刑峻法。明帝重用酷吏打击违法豪强，多次严惩贪官污吏。对宗室和勋贵犯法也严惩不贷，其姐夫梁松因罪被处死。明帝的严法政策有效整顿了吏治，但也因执法过苛而为人所批评，史家称其"法令严苛，失于宽纵"。
statement.en:
During his reign (AD 58-75), Emperor Ming departed from Emperor Guangwu's 'soft power' approach to governance, instead implementing strict laws and harsh punishments. He relied on harsh officials (Kuli) to crack down on law-breaking powerful families and repeatedly severely punished corrupt officials. He also dealt harshly with imperial clan members and nobles who broke the law, including executing his own brother-in-law, Liang Song, for his crimes. Emperor Ming's strict legal policies effectively rectified the administration of officials, but also drew criticism for excessive harshness. Historians said his 'laws were severe, lacking leniency'.

For Asia in 62 CE, “Emperor Ming Implemented Strict Laws” is a traceable node of Politics change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Vologases I Invaded Armenia

summary.en: In AD 62, Vologases I, king of the Arsacid Empire, invaded Armenia, driving out King Tigranes VI, who had been installed by Rome. Vologases placed his brother Tiridates on the Armenian throne. This sparked a Roman-Arsacid conflict over Armenia. In AD 63, the two sides concluded a treaty recognizing Tiridates as King of Armenia, but the crown was to be bestowed by Rome.

title.en: Nero Immersed Himself in Artistic Performances

summary.en: In AD 63, Roman Emperor Nero became obsessed with artistic performances. He publicly performed on stage in Rome and Naples as a lyre player and singer, forcing senators and nobles to watch and applaud. Nero's artistic hobbies coexisted with his increasingly tyrannical rule (after the Great Fire of Rome in AD 64, he built the Domus Aurea and blamed the Christians for the fire).

title.en: Emperor Ming Sent Envoys West to Seek the Dharma

summary.en: In the seventh year of the Yongping era of Eastern Han (AD 64), Emperor Ming had a dream of a golden figure flying before his palace hall. The next day, he asked his ministers. The Erudite (Boshi) Fu Yi said this was the Buddha. Therefore, the emperor dispatched the Gentleman of the Palace Cai Yin, the Imperial Academy student Qin Jing, and sixteen others on a mission to the We

statement.zh: 东汉永平七年（公元64年），汉明帝刘庄夜梦金人在殿庭中飞行，次日问群臣。博士傅毅说这是西方的佛（"佛"）。明帝因此派遣郎中蔡愔、博士弟子秦景等十八人出使西域求取佛法。这是中国历史上第一次由政府组织的西行求法活动。
statement.en:
In the seventh year of the Yongping era of Eastern Han (AD 64), Emperor Ming had a dream of a golden figure flying before his palace hall. The next day, he asked his ministers. The Erudite (Boshi) Fu Yi said this was the Buddha. Therefore, the emperor dispatched the Gentleman of the Palace Cai Yin, the Imperial Academy student Qin Jing, and sixteen others on a mission to the Western Regions to seek Buddhist scriptures. This was the first government-organized mission to seek the Dharma in Chinese history.

For Asia in 64 CE, “Emperor Ming Sent Envoys West to Seek the Dharma” is a traceable node of Religion change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Nero Built the Domus Aurea

summary.en: After the Great Fire, Nero built the lavish 'Domus Aurea' (Golden House) in the heart of Rome, covering dozens of hectares with an artificial lake, gardens, and gilded halls. Its enormous cost provoked public discontent.

statement.zh:
大火后，尼禄在罗马市中心建造奢华的“金宫”，占地数十公顷，内有人工湖、花园和镀金殿堂，耗资巨大，引发民众不满。宫殿把公共空间改为皇帝私园，走廊与穹顶装饰以壁画与黄金；财政与民怨随之紧张。金宫成为暴政的象征。

把「尼禄建造金宫」放回公元64年的罗马帝国，可以看到文化变化的一个具体切面。

title.en: Emperor Ming Pardoned the Remnants of the Chu Case

summary.en: In the eighth year of the Yongping era of Eastern Han (AD 65), the conspiracy of Liu Ying, the Prince of Chu, was exposed, implicating several thousand people. Emperor Ming was furious and used torture to extract confessions, with far-reaching repercussions. In the ninth year of Yongping, after advice from officials like Han Lang, Emperor Ming came to a realization, personally

statement.zh: 东汉永平八年（公元65年），楚王刘英谋反案发，牵连数千人。汉明帝愤怒之下严刑逼供，株连甚广。永平九年，明帝在寒朗等官员的劝谏下幡然醒悟，亲自审查案卷后赦免了大部分被牵连的无辜者。但此案仍有数百人被处死或流放。楚狱是东汉初年最大规模的诏狱案件。
statement.en:
In the eighth year of the Yongping era of Eastern Han (AD 65), the conspiracy of Liu Ying, the Prince of Chu, was exposed, implicating several 1000 people. Emperor Ming was furious and used torture to extract confessions, with far-reaching repercussions. In the ninth year of Yongping, after advice from officials like Han Lang, Emperor Ming came to a realization, personally reviewed the cases, and pardoned most of the innocent people who had been implicated. However, hundreds were still executed or exiled in this case. The Chu case was the largest in-custody case in the early Eastern Han.

For Asia in 65 CE, “Emperor Ming Pardoned the Remnants of the Chu Case” is a traceable node of Politics change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Nero Participated in the Greek Olympic Games

summary.en: Nero visited Greece, participating in the Olympic Games and the Isthmian Games at Corinth. Considering himself a genius of the arts, he was declared the winner in all competitions despite cheating. He subsequently announced the granting of autonomy and tax exemption to the Greek provinces.

statement.zh: 尼禄出访希腊，参加奥林匹克运动会和科林斯地峡运动会。他自认为艺术天才，在这些赛事中虽作弊仍被宣布为所有项目冠军；把竞技荣誉与皇帝身份绑在一起，本身就说明希腊节庆在罗马政治表达中的象征分量。随后他宣布授予希腊各行省自治权和免税权，这一举措既是回报，也是把文化亲近转化为行政安排。
statement.en: Nero visited Greece to participate in the Olympic Games and the Isthmus Games of Corinth.

statement.en: He considered himself an artistic genius, and even though he cheated in these events, he was still declared the champion in all events; tying athletic honors to the emperor's status itself illustrates the symbolic weight of Greek festivals in Roman political expression.

title.en: Cai Yin, Kasyapa Matanga Began the Journey Back East

summary.en: In the seventh year of the Yongping era (AD 64), Emperor Ming dispatched Cai Yin and seventeen others on a westward mission to seek the Dharma. Cai Yin's mission met the Indian monks Kasyapa Matanga and Dharmaratna in the state of Dayuezhi, inviting them to China. The mission loaded Buddhist images and scriptures, including the 'Sutra of Forty-Two Sections', onto a white horse

title.en: Pope Linus Became Pope

summary.en: In AD 66, Pope Linus became Bishop of Rome (Pope), succeeding the Apostle Peter. He was the second pope in Christian history. During his papacy (c. 66-78 AD), the Christian community in Rome continued to grow, but the persecution of Christians begun by Nero after the Great Fire of AD 64 was still ongoing.

statement.zh: 公元66年，圣李诺（Pope Linus）成为罗马主教（教宗），接替使徒彼得。他是基督教会历史上的第二位教宗。在位期间（约66-78年）罗马基督徒社区规模持续增长，但尼禄在公元64年大火后对基督徒的迫害仍在继续。
statement.en:
In AD 66, Pope Linus became Bishop of Rome (Pope), succeeding the Apostle Peter. He was the second pope in Christian history. During his papacy (c. 66-78 AD), the Christian community in Rome continued to grow, but the persecution of Christians begun by Nero after the Great Fire of AD 64 was still ongoing.

For Europe in 66 CE, “Pope Linus Became Pope” is a traceable node of Religion change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Outbreak of the Jewish War

summary.en: Due to the Roman governor of Judea, Gessius Florus, plundering the Temple treasury, a major rebellion erupted. The Zealots captured Jerusalem, and Rome sent troops to suppress it, marking the start of the Jewish War.

statement.zh:
犹太行省因罗马总督弗洛鲁斯劫掠圣殿财物，爆发大规模起义。奋锐党占领耶路撒冷，罗马派军镇压，犹太战争正式爆发。税收与宗教的摩擦把地方精英与下层群体推向共同反抗，圣殿与城防成为争夺焦点；战争改变了行省的治理方式。

把「犹太战争爆发」放回公元66年的罗马帝国，可以看到军事变化的一个具体切面。

title.en: Translation of the 'Sutra of Forty-Two Sections'

summary.en: Kasyapa Matanga and Dharmaratna translated the 'Sutra of Forty-Two Sections' at the White Horse Temple. It is generally considered the first Chinese translation of a Buddhist scripture, consisting of brief excerpts, and was an important document for early Buddhist transmission.

statement.zh:
摄摩腾和竺法兰在白马寺译出《四十二章经》，一般认为是中国第一部汉译佛经，内容简短摘要，是早期佛教传播的重要文献。译文以经录与问答体呈现基本教义，适应汉地阅读习惯；寺院与译经活动由此开端。它标志佛教文本进入汉语世界。

把「《四十二章经》译出」放回公元67年的东汉，可以看到文化变化的一个具体切面。

summary.en: Due to a dream of a golden figure (the Buddha), Emperor Ming of Eastern Han sent envoys west to seek the Dharma. The envoys met the Indian monks Kasyapa Matanga and Dharmaratna in the state of Dayuezhi.
