statement.zh: 东汉明帝刘庄因夜梦金人（佛陀）而遣使西域求法，使者在月氏遇到印度高僧摄摩腾和竺法兰。永平十一年（公元68年），汉明帝下令在洛阳雍门外修建白马寺以安置2位高僧和佛经。白马寺是中国第一座佛教寺院，"白马"之名源于佛经曾由白马驮载而来。寺内建有中国最早的佛塔和译经场所。摄摩腾和竺法兰在此翻译了《四十二章经》，是中国最早的汉语佛经。
statement.en:
Due to a dream of a golden figure (the Buddha), Emperor Ming of Eastern Han sent envoys west to seek the Dharma. The envoys met the Indian monks Kasyapa Matanga and Dharmaratna in the state of Dayuezhi. In the eleventh year of the Yongping era (AD 68), Emperor Ming ordered the construction of the White Horse Temple outside the Yongmen Gate in Luoyang to house the two monks and the Buddhist scriptures. This was the first Buddhist temple in China, named 'White Horse' because the scriptures had been carried on a white horse. The temple housed the earliest Buddhist pagoda and scripture translation center in China, where Kasyapa Matanga and Dharmaratna translated the 'Sutra of 42 Sections', the first Chinese translation of a Buddhist scripture.

For Asia in 68 CE, “Expansion of the White Horse Temple” is a traceable node of Religion change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Wang Jing Ordered to Harness the Yellow River

summary.en: The Yellow River had breached its banks and flooded for years. Emperor Ming sent Wang Jing and Wang Wu to tame the Yellow River. Wang Jing used a combination of techniques including levee construction, diversion, and dredging, keeping the river stable for over 800 years.

statement.zh:
黄河决口泛滥数年，汉明帝派王景和王吴治理黄河。王景采用筑堤、分洪、疏浚等综合措施，使黄河安流八百余年。工程先测地形与水势，再修堤束水、开渠分洪，并疏浚旧河道；治河之后，泛区恢复农耕，漕运也得以畅通。

把「王景奉命治理黄河」放回公元69年的东汉，可以看到工程变化的一个具体切面。
statement.en: The Yellow River had breached its banks and flooded for years.

title.en: The Second Temple of Jerusalem is destroyed

summary.en: Rome crushed the Jewish revolt and razed the Second Temple, leaving only the Western Wall, for centuries a place of mourning and pilgrimage for the Jewish people.

statement.zh: 罗马镇压犹太起义，夷平第二圣殿，仅余西墙（哭墙），成为犹太民族1000年哀恸与朝圣之地。圣殿被夷平，意味着祭祀中心与政治象征同时消失；而西墙的残存又把毁灭转化为一个可以持续凭吊的地点。建筑上的“只剩一段墙”，在宗教与民族记忆中反而成为最完整的象征。
statement.en:
Rome suppressed the Jewish uprising and razed the Second Temple, leaving only the Western Wall (Wailing Wall), which became a place of mourning and pilgrimage for the Jewish people for thousands of years. The razing of the temple meant that both the sacrificial center and the political symbol disappeared at the same time; and the remnants of the Western Wall transformed the destruction into a place where one can continue to pay tribute. "Only a section of wall" remains in the building, but it has become the most complete symbol in religious and national memory.

It sits within the timeline's chronological coverage of Judea and architecture history.

title.en: Beginning of the Rabbinic Era in Judaism

summary.en: After the destruction of the Temple, Judaism lost its sacrificial center. Rabbi Yohanan ben Zakkai established an academy at Yavneh, developing Rabbinic Judaism. Judaism centered on law and the synagogue has continued to this day.

statement.zh:
圣殿被毁后，犹太教失去祭祀中心，拉比约哈南·本·扎卡伊在亚夫内建立学院，发展拉比犹太教，以律法和会堂为中心的犹太教延续至今。学院以口传律法与经典注释维系信仰，会堂取代圣殿成为礼拜与社群生活的中心；拉比权威在流散中确立。犹太教形态由此转型。

把「犹太教拉比时代开启」放回公元70年的犹太，可以看到宗教变化的一个具体切面。

title.en: Wang Jing Successfully Tamed the Yellow River

summary.en: In the thirteenth year of the Yongping era of Eastern Han (AD 70), the large-scale project by hydraulic engineer Wang Jing to tame the Yellow River and the Bian Canal was fully completed. Wang Jing employed a comprehensive strategy involving levee construction, cutting off meanders, and building sluice gates. He mobilized hundreds of thousands of laborers at a cost of tens of b

statement.zh: 东汉永平十三年（公元70年），水利专家王景治理黄河和汴渠的工程全面完工。王景采用筑堤、裁弯取直、修建水门（闸门）等综合方案，动员数十万民夫，工程费用达数百亿钱。完工后黄河在接下来的八百年间（至北宋中期）没有发生大规模改道，是黄河治理史上最成功的工程之一。
statement.en:
In the thirteenth year of the Yongping era of Eastern Han (AD 70), the large-scale project by hydraulic engineer Wang Jing to tame the Yellow River and the Bian Canal was fully completed. Wang Jing employed a comprehensive strategy involving levee construction, cutting off meanders, and building sluice gates. He mobilized 100,000 of laborers at a cost of tens of billions of cash. After completion, the Yellow River did not undergo a major course change for the next 800 years (until the mid-Northern Song dynasty), making this one of the most successful river control projects in history.

For Asia in 70 CE, “Wang Jing Successfully Tamed the Yellow River” is a traceable node of Engineering change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Vespasian Built the Roman Colosseum

summary.en: Vespasian ordered the construction of the Roman Colosseum (Flavian Amphitheatre) on the site of Nero's Domus Aurea's artificial lake. It became the largest amphitheatre in the Roman Empire, capable of seating 50,000 spectators.

statement.zh: 韦斯帕芗下令在尼禄金宫的人工湖旧址上建造罗马斗兽场（弗拉维圆形剧场），成为罗马帝国最大竞技场，可容纳5万观众。建筑以混凝土与砖石拱券层层叠起，看台、通道与地下室组织出复杂的观演空间；它把私人园苑改建为公众娱乐的场所，宣示新王朝与民同乐。竞技与庆典在此上演。
statement.en: Vespasian ordered the construction of the Colosseum (Flavian Amphitheater) on the site of the artificial lake in Nero's Golden Palace, which became the largest arena in the Roman Empire and could accommodate 50,000 spectators.

title.en: Titus Returned to Rome and Celebrated a Triumph

title.en: Emperor Ming Ordered Ban Chao to Prepare to Communicate with the Western Regions

summary.en: In the fifteenth year of the Yongping era of Eastern Han (AD 72), Emperor Ming appointed Ban Chao as Acting Major (Jia Sima) and sent him with 36 men on a mission to the Western Regions. Ban Chao showed bravery in battle at Pulei Hai (Barkol Lake), earning the appreciation of Dou Gu. He subsequently convinced the kingdoms of Shanshan and Khotan to submit to the Eastern Han, reo

statement.zh: 东汉永平十五年（公元72年），汉明帝命班超为假司马率三十六人出使西域。班超在蒲类海一役中奋勇杀敌获窦固赏识。他先后说服鄯善、于阗归附东汉，以"不入虎穴焉得虎子"的胆略重开西域通路。
statement.en:
In the fifteenth year of the Yongping era of Eastern Han (AD 72), Emperor Ming appointed Ban Chao as Acting Major (Jia Sima) and sent him with 36 men on a mission to the Western Regions. Ban Chao showed bravery in battle at Pulei Hai (Barkol Lake), earning the appreciation of Dou Gu. He subsequently convinced the kingdoms of Shanshan and Khotan to submit to the Eastern Han, reopening the route to the Western Regions with his courageous action, 'How can you catch tiger cubs without entering the tiger's lair?'

For Asia in 72 CE, “Emperor Ming Ordered Ban Chao to Prepare to Communicate with the Western Regions” is a traceable node of Military change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Ban Chao's Mission to the Western Regions: 'How Can You Catch Tiger Cubs Without Entering the Tiger's Lair?'

summary.en: Dou Gu sent Ban Chao with 36 men on a mission to the southern route of the Western Regions. First arriving at Shanshan (Loulan), Ban Chao inspired his men with the words 'How can you catch tiger cubs without entering the tiger's lair?' and led a night raid on the camp of the Xiongnu envoys, killing over a hundred, forcing the king of Shanshan to submit to the Han dynasty.

statement.en: Reaching Shanshan, that is Loulan, Ban Chao inspired his men with the words 'How can you catch tiger cubs without entering the tiger's lair?' and led a night raid on the Xiongnu envoys' camp, killing over a hundred and forcing the king of Shanshan to submit to Han.

title.en: Fall of Masada Fortress

summary.en: The last stronghold of the Jewish resistance, Masada fortress, was captured by the Roman 10th Legion. All of the approximately 960 defenders committed suicide, becoming a symbol of the indomitable spirit of the Jewish people.

statement.zh:
犹太战争中最后一个抵抗据点马萨达要塞被罗马第十军团攻陷。守军约960人全部自杀，成为犹太民族不屈精神的象征。山地要塞依托陡崖与蓄水池固守，罗马以土坡与攻城塔强攻；陷落后的集体殉难被后世反复记忆。要塞此后只余遗址。

title.en: Ban Chao Subdued Shule (Kashgar)

summary.en: In AD 74, Ban Chao first arrived at Gepantuo (modern Taxkorgan, Xinjiang), then from a small path entered Shule (modern Kashgar, Xinjiang). He sent his subordinate, Tian Lü, to kidnap the pro-Xiongnu King Douti of Shule, establishing the former king's nephew, Zhong, as the new king of Shule. From then on, Ban Chao used Shule as his base to manage the Western Regions.

summary.en: In AD 75, Emperor Ming of Han died of illness in the front hall of the Eastern Palace in Luoyang, after an eighteen-year reign. statement.en:
In AD 75, Emperor Ming of Han died of illness in the front hall of the Eastern Palace in Luoyang, after an eighteen-year reign. His crown prince, Liu Da, ascended the throne (Emperor Zhang of Han), at the age of 19. During Emperor Ming's reign, official administration was honest and upright, the frontiers were secure, and his dispatch of envoys west to seek the Dharma led to the official introduction of Buddhism to China. Emperor Zhang continued to pursue benevolent and lenient policies.

For Asia in 75 CE, “Emperor Ming of Han Died, Emperor Zhang Ascended” is a traceable node of Politics change whose significance is best read through later events.

en: In AD 75, Emperor Ming of Han died of illness in the front hall of the Eastern Palace in Luoyang, after an eighteen-year reign. His crown prince, Liu Da, ascended the throne (Emperor Zhang of Han), at the age of 19. During Emperor Ming's reign, official administration was honest and upright, the frontiers were secure, and his dispatch of envoys west to seek the Dharma led to the official introduction of Buddhism to China. Emperor Zhang continued to pursue benevolent and lenient policies.

title.en: Geng Gong Held Out in the Western Regions

summary.en: In 75-76 CE Geng Gong, the Eastern Han Wuji Colonel, held the fortress of Shule in the Western Regions — near modern Qitai in Xinjiang, a different place from the Shule kingdom at Kashgar — with a few dozen soldiers against a siege by the Northern Xiongnu and their Jushi allies. When the food ran out his men boiled the hide and sinew of their armour and crossbow strings to eat,

statement.zh: 公元75至76年，东汉戊己校尉耿恭率数十名汉军困守西域疏勒城（在今新疆奇台一带，与喀什的疏勒国同名而异地）。抵御北匈奴与车师联军的围攻。城中粮尽，将士煮铠甲、弩弦上的筋革充饥；井深十五丈不出水，耿恭整衣拜井，终得泉涌。汉章帝建初元年（76年）遣酒泉太守段彭、谒者王蒙等率七千余人出玉门关驰援，破车师、解疏勒之围。援军抵达时守军仅余二十六人，东归至玉门关时只剩十三人，史称"十三将士归玉门"。
statement.en: In 75-76 CE Geng Gong, the Eastern Han Wuji Colonel, held the fortress of Shule in the Western Regions — near modern Qitai in Xinjiang, a different place from the Shule kingdom at Kashgar — with a few dozen soldiers against a siege by the Northern Xiongnu and their Jushi allies. When the food ran out his men boiled the hide and sinew of their armour and crossbow strings to eat, and a well sunk more than thirty metres finally yielded water. In 76 Emperor Zhang sent the governor of Jiuquan, Duan Peng, and the envoy Wang Meng with over seven thousand men out through the Jade Gate to relieve them. Only 26 defenders were still alive when the relief force arrived, and thirteen reached the Jade Gate — remembered as "the thirteen who came back to the Jade Gate".

zh: 公元75至76年，东汉戊己校尉耿恭率数十名汉军困守西域疏勒城（在今新疆奇台一带，与喀什的疏勒国同名而异地）。抵御北匈奴与车师联军的围攻。城中粮尽，将士煮铠甲、弩弦上的筋革充饥；井深十五丈不出水，耿恭整衣拜井，终得泉涌。汉章帝建初元年（76年）遣酒泉太守段彭、谒者王蒙等率七千余人出玉门关驰援，破车师、解疏勒之围。援军抵达时守军仅余二十六人，东归至玉门关时只剩十三人，史称"十三将士归玉门"。

title.en: White Tiger Pavilion Conference and the 'Baihu Tongyi'

summary.en: Emperor Zhang convened a conference on the classics at the White Tiger Pavilion (Baihu Guan) to discuss discrepancies in the Five Classics. Ban Gu was ordered to compile the records of the conference, resulting in the 'Baihu Tongyi' (Comprehensive Discussions in the White Tiger Pavilion), which unified Confucian classical thought.

汉章帝在白虎观召开经学会议，讨论五经异同。班固奉命整理会议记录，编成《白虎通义》，统一儒家经学思想。会议汇集博士与儒生，就经义、礼制与政治秩序展开辩论，最后由皇帝裁定；成书以问答体归纳条目，成为官方经学的依据。

title.en: Mount Vesuvius Erupted, Burying Pompeii

summary.en: On August 24, Mount Vesuvius erupted violently, burying cities such as Pompeii and Herculaneum under pumice and ash within hours. Approximately 20,000 people perished. The cities were perfectly preserved, providing invaluable insights into Roman life.

statement.zh:
8月24日，维苏威火山猛烈爆发，火山灰和浮石在数小时内掩埋庞贝、赫库兰尼姆等城市，约两万人遇难。灾难的破坏与保存是同一过程的两面：火山碎屑迅速封存街巷、住宅与日常器物，使这些城市在后来发掘中成为观察古罗马生活最直接的样本。

把「罗马维苏威火山爆发，庞贝古城被埋」放回公元79年的罗马帝国，可以看到灾难变化的一个具体切面。
statement.en: On August 24, Mount Vesuvius violently erupted.

title.en: Wang Chong writes the Lunheng

summary.en: The Eastern Han philosopher Wang Chong writes the Lunheng, using naturalism to critique occult prophecies and the mandate of heaven.

statement.zh: 东汉哲学家王充撰《论衡》，以元气自然论批判谶纬神学与天人感应，主张以实知验证虚妄。他把万物生成归于元气的聚散，否认天有意志、能以灾异谴告人；对当时流行的谶纬与神异传说，他逐条追问证据，强调见闻与效验。这种怀疑与实证的态度在汉代思想中颇为异类，后世常以“疾虚妄”概括其精神。

title.en: The Colosseum opens: public entertainment and imperial finance

summary.en: Construction of the Flavian Amphitheatre began under Vespasian in 70–72 CE; Titus dedicated it in 80 with 100 days of games, and Domitian added the fourth story in 82. About 189 by 156 metres and holding as many as 50,000 spectators, it was paid for with the spoils of Jerusalem in 70 and built by enslaved Jews from Judaea.

statement.zh: 罗马斗兽场，又称弗拉维安露天剧场，在弗拉维王朝的韦帕芗手中于公元70–72年间动工。提图斯在80年主持落成典礼，庆典包括100天比赛；图密善在82年加建第四层。
statement.en: The Colosseum, also called the Flavian Amphitheatre, was begun under the Flavian emperor Vespasian between 70 and 72 CE. Titus dedicated it in 80 CE with 100 days of games, and Domitian added the fourth story in 82 CE.

sources.excerpt: Construction of the Colosseum began under the Roman emperor Vespasian between 70 and 72 CE. The completed structure was dedicated in 80 CE by Titus, Vespasian’s son and successor. The Colosseum’s fourth story was added by the emperor Domitian in 82 CE. Importantly, the arena was paid for with plunder from Titus’s sack of Jerusalem in 70 CE, and it was built by enslaved Jewish people from Judaea.
The structure was officially dedicated in 80 CE by Titus in a ceremony that included 100 days of games.

zh: 罗马斗兽场，又称弗拉维安露天剧场，在弗拉维王朝的韦帕芗手中于公元70–72年间动工。
提图斯在80年主持落成典礼，庆典包括100天比赛；图密善在82年加建第四层。
en: The Colosseum, also called the Flavian Amphitheatre, was begun under the Flavian emperor Vespasian between 70 and 72 CE.
Titus dedicated it in 80 CE with 100 days of games, and Domitian added the fourth story in 82 CE.

note.zh: 动工、落成、第四层三个时间点分开写。
note.en: Construction, dedication and the fourth story are kept as three distinct dates.

statement.zh: 斗兽场是椭圆形建筑，用石、混凝土与凝灰岩建成，最高处四层，长宽为189×156米，可容纳多达约50,000名观众。
statement.en: It is an elliptical structure of stone, concrete and tuff, four stories high, measuring 189 by 156 metres and holding as many as 50,000 spectators.

sources.excerpt: The Colosseum is an amphitheater built in Rome under the Flavian emperors of the Roman Empire. It is also called the Flavian Amphitheatre. It is an elliptical structure made of stone, concrete, and tuff, and it stands four stories tall at its highest point. It measures 620 by 513 feet (189 by 156 meters) and could hold as many as 50,000 spectators.

zh: 斗兽场是椭圆形建筑，用石、混凝土与凝灰岩建成，最高处四层，长宽为189×156米，可容纳多达约50,000名观众。
en: It is an elliptical structure of stone, concrete and tuff, four stories high, measuring 189 by 156 metres and holding as many as 50,000 spectators.

note.zh: 容量写“多达约50,000”，不写固定八万。
note.en: Capacity is 'as many as 50,000', not a fixed 80,000.

statement.zh: 它的经费来自提图斯70年洗劫耶路撒冷的战利品，建造者是来自犹太地的被奴役犹太人；选址在尼禄金宫的人工湖上，把皇帝的私人园林改成公共剧场。
statement.en: It was paid for with the spoils of Titus's sack of Jerusalem in 70 CE and built by enslaved Jewish people from Judaea; it was sited on the artificial lake of Nero's Golden House, replacing a private imperial pleasure ground with a public amphitheatre.

sources.excerpt: Construction of the Colosseum began under the Roman emperor Vespasian between 70 and 72 CE. The completed structure was dedicated in 80 CE by Titus, Vespasian’s son and successor. The Colosseum’s fourth story was added by the emperor Domitian in 82 CE. Importantly, the arena was paid for with plunder from Titus’s sack of Jerusalem in 70 CE, and it was built by enslaved Jewish people from Judaea.

It is located just east of the Palatine Hill, on the grounds of what was Nero’s Golden House. The artificial lake that was the centerpiece of that palace complex was drained, and the Colosseum was sited there, a decision that was as much symbolic as it was practical. Vespasian, whose path to the throne had relatively humble beginnings, chose to replace the tyrannical emperor’s private lake with a public amphitheater that could host tens of thousands of Romans.

zh: 它的经费来自提图斯70年洗劫耶路撒冷的战利品，建造者是来自犹太地的被奴役犹太人；选址在尼禄金宫的人工湖上，把皇帝的私人园林改成公共剧场。
en: It was paid for with the spoils of Titus's sack of Jerusalem in 70 CE and built by enslaved Jewish people from Judaea; it was sited on the artificial lake of Nero's Golden House, replacing a private imperial pleasure ground with a public amphitheatre.

note.zh: 经费、建造者与选址照条目；不写“全部由战俘建造”。
note.en: Funding, builders and site follow the entry; no claim that all workers were prisoners of war.

statement.zh: 这里举行角斗士搏斗、猎兽和模拟海战；观众席上方有可伸缩的遮阳篷，由水手操作。
statement.en: It hosted gladiatorial combat, animal hunts and mock naval battles; a retractable awning above the seating was worked by sailors.

sources.locator: Britannica, Colosseum, 'Why was the Colosseum built?'
sources.excerpt: The Colosseum was built as part of an imperial effort to revitalize Rome after the tumultuous year of the four emperors, 69 CE. As with other amphitheaters, the emperor Vespasian intended the Colosseum to be an entertainment venue, hosting gladiator fights, animal hunts, and even mock naval battles.
The amphitheater seated some 50,000 spectators, who were shielded from the sun by a massive retractable velarium (awning).

zh: 这里举行角斗士搏斗、猎兽和模拟海战；观众席上方有可伸缩的遮阳篷，由水手操作。
en: It hosted gladiatorial combat, animal hunts and mock naval battles; a retractable awning above the seating was worked by sailors.

note.zh: 三种用途与遮阳篷照条目；不写“基督徒被喂狮”。
note.en: The three uses and the awning follow the entry; no 'Christians fed to lions' detail.

statement.zh: 斗兽场不只是工程奇迹，也是皇帝用公共娱乐换取声望的装置；它的建造与维护都依赖帝国的财政与奴隶劳动。
statement.en: The Colosseum was not only an engineering marvel but also a device through which the emperor converted public entertainment into prestige; its construction and upkeep depended on imperial finance and slave labour.

en: The Colosseum was not only an engineering marvel but also a device through which the emperor converted public entertainment into prestige; its construction and upkeep depended on imperial finance and slave labour.

note.zh: 作者判断：把公共娱乐当作政治语言，不把工程奇迹当成中立事实。
note.en: Author judgment: public entertainment as political language, not neutral engineering.

title.en: Ban Chao Memorialized Requesting Troops to Attack Kucha

summary.en: In the third year of the Yuanhe era (AD 83), Ban Chao, Protector General of the Western Regions, memorialized Emperor Zhang requesting reinforcements to attack and destroy the state of Kucha (modern Kuqa, Xinjiang). In his memorial, Ban Chao pointed out that Kucha was the largest ally of the Northern Xiongnu in the Western Regions, and destroying Kucha would fully open the nort

statement.zh: 东汉元和三年（公元83年），西域都护班超向汉章帝上书请求增兵以攻灭龟兹国（今新疆库车）。班超在奏疏中指出龟兹是北匈奴在西域的最大盟友，攻灭龟兹即可彻底打通西域北道。章帝应允派遣援军1000人，并任命班超为将兵长史。班超随后率汉军和西域联军攻破龟兹城，迫使其退出北匈奴联盟。这场胜利最终确立了东汉对西域的完全控制。
statement.en:
In the third year of the Yuanhe era (AD 83), Ban Chao, Protector General of the Western Regions, memorialized Emperor Zhang requesting reinforcements to attack and destroy the state of Kucha (modern Kuqa, Xinjiang). In his memorial, Ban Chao pointed out that Kucha was the largest ally of the Northern Xiongnu in the Western Regions, and destroying Kucha would fully open the northern route of the Western Regions. Emperor Zhang approved the request, sending 1,000 reinforcements and appointing Ban Chao as General of the Long History (Jiangbing Zhangshi). Ban Chao then led Han forces and allied Western Regions armies to capture Kucha City, forcing it to withdraw from the Northern Xiongnu alliance. This victory ultimately established the Eastern Han's complete control over the Western Regions.

For Asia in 83 CE, “Ban Chao Memorialized Requesting Troops to Attack Kucha” is a traceable node of Military change whose significance is best read through later events.

statement.zh: 东汉元和二年（公元85年），汉章帝采纳编訢、李梵等人的历法改革建议，正式颁布施行《四分历》。

title.en: Eastern Han Formally Implemented the Sexagenary Cycle

summary.en: Emperor Zhang, adopting the proposals of scholars such as Li Fan and Bian Xin, issued an edict formally implementing the sexagenary cycle (stem-branch calendar) nationwide. This system, with a cycle of sixty years (one Jiazi), has been continuously used ever since, making it the oldest continuously used calendar system in the world.

statement.zh:
汉章帝采纳李梵、编䜣等学者建议，下诏在全国正式推行干支纪年法，六十年一甲子，连续使用至今，是世界上最古老的连续纪年系统。天干地支循环组合，把年份纳入可推算的序列；纪年统一便利了官方文书与历法。传统时间观念由此制度化。

把「东汉正式推行干支纪年」放回公元85年的东汉，可以看到文化变化的一个具体切面。

title.en: Unification of the Dacian Kingdom

summary.en: Between about AD 82 and 86 the Dacian king Decebalus unified the Dacian tribes (modern Romania). He built a powerful army and raised a network of fortresses in the Orastie Mountains. In AD 85-86 he crossed the Danube into the Roman province of Moesia and killed its governor, Oppius Sabinus, sparking the Roman-Dacian War of AD 86-89.

statement.en: Between about 82 CE and 86 the Dacian king Decebalus unified the Dacian tribes (modern Romania).

title.en: Domitian's Dacian wars

summary.en: Between AD 86 and 89 Rome fought a series of wars against the kingdom of Dacia, in what is now Romania, on the lower Danube. King Decebalus crossed the river into Moesia and killed its governor Oppius Sabinus; the following year the praetorian prefect Cornelius Fuscus led a punitive expedition that was annihilated. In 88 the general Tettius Julianus crushed the Dacians at Tapae

statement.zh: 公元86至89年，罗马与达契亚王国（今罗马尼亚）在多瑙河下游爆发一系列战争。达契亚国王德凯巴鲁斯率军越过多瑙河突入默西亚行省，总督奥庇乌斯·萨比努斯战死。次年禁卫军长官科尔内利乌斯·富斯库斯统兵反击，亦遭全军覆没。88年，将领特提乌斯·尤利安努斯在塔佩大破达契亚军，扳回败局。但日耳曼边境同时告急，图密善急于抽调兵力，遂于89年与德凯巴鲁斯媾和，以年金和罗马工匠技师换取其名义上的臣服。此役暴露了罗马多瑙河防线的脆弱，也为图拉真日后彻底征服达契亚埋下伏笔。
statement.en: Between 86 CE and 89 Rome fought a series of wars against the kingdom of Dacia, in what is now Romania, on the lower Danube.

title.en: Emperor Zhang of Han Died, Emperor He Ascended

summary.en: In AD 88, Emperor Zhang of Han died of illness in the Zhangde Front Hall at Luoyang. His ten-year-old crown prince, Liu Zhao, ascended the throne (Emperor He of Han). Empress Dowager Dou assumed regency (Lin Chao Chen Zhi), and her brother Dou Xian served as Grand General (Da Jiangjun) assisting in governance. The Dou clan consort kin began to dominate the court, marking the be

statement.zh: 公元88年，汉章帝刘炟病逝于洛阳章德前殿。年仅十岁的太子刘肇即位（汉和帝）。窦太后临朝称制，其兄窦宪以大将军身份辅政，窦氏外戚开始把持朝政，东汉进入外戚与宦官交替专权的时期。
statement.en:
In AD 88, Emperor Zhang of Han died of illness in the Zhangde Front Hall at Luoyang. His ten-year-old crown prince, Liu Zhao, ascended the throne (Emperor He of Han). Empress Dowager Dou assumed regency (Lin Chao Chen Zhi), and her brother Dou Xian served as Grand General (Da Jiangjun) assisting in governance. The Dou clan consort kin began to dominate the court, marking the beginning of an era of alternating eunuch and consort kin domination in the Eastern Han.

For Asia in 88 CE, “Emperor Zhang of Han Died, Emperor He Ascended” is a traceable node of Politics change whose significance is best read through later events.

zh: 公元88年，汉章帝刘炟病逝于洛阳章德前殿。年仅十岁的太子刘肇即位（汉和帝）。窦太后临朝称制，其兄窦宪以大将军身份辅政，窦氏外戚开始把持朝政，东汉进入外戚与宦官交替专权的时期。
公元88年，汉章帝刘炟病逝于洛阳章德前殿。
en: In AD 88, Emperor Zhang of Han died of illness in the Zhangde Front Hall at Luoyang. His ten-year-old crown prince, Liu Zhao, ascended the throne (Emperor He of Han). Empress Dowager Dou assumed regency (Lin Chao Chen Zhi), and her brother Dou Xian served as Grand General (Da Jiangjun) assisting in governance. The Dou clan consort kin began to dominate the court, marking the beginning of an era of alternating eunuch and consort kin domination in the Eastern Han.
In AD 88, Emperor Zhang of Han died of illness in the Zhangde Front Hall at Luoyang.

title.en: Northern Xiongnu Sent Envoys to Submit

summary.en: In the second year of the Yongyuan era of Eastern Han (AD 90), the Northern Xiongnu, severely weakened by the successive attacks of Dou Xian and Geng Bing, sent envoys to Luoyang to submit to the Eastern Han. Emperor He accepted the Northern Xiongnu's request for submission, requiring them to send their sons to the capital as hostages and to pay annual tribute to the Han court.

statement.zh: 东汉永元二年（公元90年），北匈奴在窦宪、耿秉等汉将的连续打击下元气大伤，单于遣使至洛阳向东汉称臣。和帝接受北匈奴的归附请求，要求其遣子入侍为质并每年向汉朝进贡。北匈奴的衰落和归附标志着汉匈百年战争的转折点，此后北匈奴残余势力逐渐西迁，南匈奴则继续在东汉边境游牧。
statement.en:
In the second year of the Yongyuan era of Eastern Han (AD 90), the Northern Xiongnu, severely weakened by the successive attacks of Dou Xian and Geng Bing, sent envoys to Luoyang to submit to the Eastern Han. Emperor He accepted the Northern Xiongnu's request for submission, requiring them to send their sons to the capital as hostages and to pay annual tribute to the Han court. The decline and submission of the Northern Xiongnu marked a turning point in the centuries-old Han-Xiongnu wars. After this, the remnants of the Northern Xiongnu gradually migrated westward, while the Southern Xiongnu continued to roam the frontier regions of the Eastern Han.

For Asia in 90 CE, “Northern Xiongnu Sent Envoys to Submit” is a traceable node of Diplomacy change whose significance is best read through later events.

statement.zh: 东汉永元四年（公元92年），汉和帝铲除窦宪势力后，班固受牵连被下狱。班固曾为窦宪的幕僚，在窦宪失势后被洛阳令逮捕入狱，同年死在狱中，享年61岁。班固的《汉书》未完成的部分由班昭续写。
statement.en:
In the fourth year of the Yongyuan era of Eastern Han (AD 92), after Emperor He purged Dou Xian's faction, Ban Gu was implicated and imprisoned. Ban Gu had served as a staff member of Dou Xian. After Dou Xian fell from power, Ban Gu was arrested by the Prefect of Luoyang and died in prison the same year, at the age of 61. The unfinished portions of Ban Gu's 'Book of Han' were completed by his sister Ban Zhao.

For Asia in 92 CE, “Ban Gu Imprisoned and Died Due to Association with Dou Xian” is a traceable node of Culture change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Emperor He Eliminated Dou Xian's Faction

summary.en: The fourteen-year-old Emperor He of Han, conspiring with the eunuch Zheng Zhong, staged a coup to arrest Dou Xian and his faction. title.en: Josephus Wrote 'Antiquities of the Jews'

summary.en: The Jewish historian Josephus completed 'Antiquities of the Jews', a detailed account of Jewish history from creation to the Jewish War. It is an important source for the study of Jewish and early Christian history.

statement.zh: 公元93年，汉和帝刘肇在宦官郑众帮助下成功铲除窦宪势力后开始亲政。和帝勤于政务，多次下诏减免赋税、赈济灾民，并重新选拔贤能的官员管理朝政。东汉国力和声誉在其统治下持续上升。
statement.en:
In AD 93, after successfully eliminating Dou Xian's faction with the help of the eunuch Zheng Zhong, Emperor He began to rule personally. He was diligent in state affairs, repeatedly issuing edicts to reduce taxes and provide relief to disaster victims. He also re-selected capable and virtuous officials to manage the court. The Eastern Han's national strength and prestige continued to rise during his reign.

For Asia in 93 CE, “Emperor He Ruled Personally, Striving for Good Governance” is a traceable node of Politics change whose significance is best read through later events.

title.en: Ban Chao Pacified Yānqí

summary.en: Ban Chao led allied Western Regions forces to attack the kingdom of Yānqí (which had previously killed a Han protector general). Ban Chao captured and killed the king of Yānqí through a stratagem, pacifying Yānqí. With this, all fifty-plus kingdoms of the Western Regions submitted to the Eastern Han.

title.en: Domitian is assassinated; Nerva adopts Trajan

summary.en: On September 18, 96 CE Domitian was killed in a palace conspiracy involving the praetorian prefects, court officials and the empress; the Senate welcomed Nerva as emperor. The guard forced Nerva to punish the assassins, and frontier commanders were discontented. In October 97 Nerva adopted Trajan, governor of Upper Germany; when Nerva died in January 98, Trajan was accepted by

statement.zh: 96年9月18日，图密善在宫廷阴谋中被杀。阴谋由两名禁卫军长官、若干宫廷官员和皇后多米提亚·隆吉娜主导，涅尔瓦很可能知情。
statement.en: On September 18, 96 CE, Domitian was killed in a palace conspiracy. The plot was led by the two praetorian prefects, court officials and the empress Domitia Longina; Nerva was probably privy to it.

sources.locator: Britannica, Domitian, 'Domitian’s reign of terror and assassination'
sources.excerpt: The conspiracy that caused his murder on September 18, 96, was led by the two praetorian prefects, various palace officials, and the emperor’s wife, Domitia Longina (daughter of Gnaeus Domitius Corbulo). Nerva who took over the government at once, must clearly have been privy. The Senate was overjoyed at Domitian’s death, and his memory was officially condemned, but the army took it badly; the next year they insisted on the punishment of those responsible.

zh: 96年9月18日，图密善在宫廷阴谋中被杀。
阴谋由两名禁卫军长官、若干宫廷官员和皇后多米提亚·隆吉娜主导，涅尔瓦很可能知情。
en: On September 18, 96 CE, Domitian was killed in a palace conspiracy.
The plot was led by the two praetorian prefects, court officials and the empress Domitia Longina; Nerva was probably privy to it.

note.zh: 参与者与“很可能知情”照条目，不写成涅尔瓦亲自动手。
note.en: Participants and 'probably privy' follow the entry; Nerva is not made the assassin.

statement.zh: 元老院对图密善之死表示欢迎，并正式谴责他的记忆；军队反应相反，次年要求惩处凶手。
statement.en: The Senate welcomed Domitian's death and officially condemned his memory; the army reacted badly and the next year demanded punishment of those responsible.

sources.locator: Britannica, Domitian, 'Domitian’s reign of terror and assassination'
sources.excerpt: The conspiracy that caused his murder on September 18, 96, was led by the two praetorian prefects, various palace officials, and the emperor’s wife, Domitia Longina (daughter of Gnaeus Domitius Corbulo). Nerva who took over the government at once, must clearly have been privy. The Senate was overjoyed at Domitian’s death, and his memory was officially condemned, but the army took it badly; the next year they insisted on the punishment of those responsible.

zh:
96年9月18日，图密善在宫廷阴谋中被杀。阴谋由两名禁卫军长官、若干宫廷官员和皇后多米提亚·隆吉娜主导，涅尔瓦很可能知情。

元老院对图密善之死表示欢迎，并正式谴责他的记忆；军队反应相反，次年要求惩处凶手。

title.en: Gan Ying Sent on a Mission to Great Qin (Roman Empire)

summary.en: Ban Chao sent Gan Ying on a mission to Great Qin (the Roman Empire). Gan Ying traveled through the Arsacid (Parthian) Empire, reaching the Persian Gulf. As he was preparing to cross the sea, Parthian merchants advised him against it, citing the dangerous and lengthy sea journey. Gan Ying had no choice but to return, never reaching Rome.

title.en: Emperor He Deposed Empress Dowager Dou

summary.en: In the ninth year of the Yongyuan era (AD 97), after eliminating Dou Xian's faction with the help of the eunuch Zheng Zhong, Emperor He issued an edict deposing Empress Dowager Dou of her title and posthumously demeaning her to commoner status. statement.zh: 东汉和帝刘肇在宦官郑众的帮助下铲除窦宪势力后，于永元九年（公元97年）下诏废去窦太后的尊号，追贬为庶人。窦太后是窦宪的妹妹，在章帝去世后以太后身份临朝听政，窦氏家族把持朝政十余年。和帝在郑众等宦官协助下发动政变，解除窦宪大将军职务迫其自杀，窦氏势力遭到彻底清算，结束了东汉第一次外戚专权局面。
statement.en:
In the ninth year of the Yongyuan era (AD 97), after eliminating Dou Xian's faction with the help of the eunuch Zheng Zhong, Emperor He issued an edict deposing Empress Dowager Dou of her title and posthumously demeaning her to commoner status. Empress Dowager Dou was the sister of Dou Xian, who had assumed regency after Emperor Zhang's death, allowing the Dou clan to dominate the court for over a decade. With the help of eunuchs like Zheng Zhong, Emperor He launched a coup, removing Dou Xian from his post as Grand General and forcing him to commit suicide. The Dou clan's power was thoroughly liquidated, ending the first period of consort kin domination in the Eastern Han.

For Asia in 97 CE, “Emperor He Deposed Empress Dowager Dou” is a traceable node of Politics change whose significance is best read through later events.

statement.zh: 东汉永元十一年（公元99年），年迈的班超上疏汉和帝请求返回中原。他在奏章中写道："臣不敢望到酒泉郡，但愿生入玉门关。"他的妹妹班昭也上书请求准许班超归国。和帝被感动，下诏征班超回京。班超于公元100年回到洛阳。
statement.en:
In the eleventh year of the Yongyuan era of Eastern Han (AD 99), the aged Ban Chao memorialized Emperor He, requesting permission to return to the Central Plains. In his memorial, he wrote: 'I dare not hope to reach Jiuquan, only that I may live to enter the Jade Gate Pass.' His sister Ban Zhao also submitted a memorial requesting that Ban Chao be allowed to return. Moved by these appeals, the Emperor issued an edict summoning Ban Chao back to the capital. Ban Chao returned to Luoyang in AD 100.

title.en: Ban Chao Returned to Luoyang and Died

summary.en: Ban Chao returned to Luoyang, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Dingyuan, and soon died of illness at the age of 71. He had operated in the Western Regions for 31 years, bringing over fifty kingdoms into submission to the Eastern Han and reopening the Silk Road.

statement.zh: 班超回到洛阳，受封定远侯，不久病逝，享年71岁。他在西域活动31年，以使者、屯田与联姻结好诸国，使西域五十余国归附，重新开通丝绸之路。班超以少数吏士周旋于绿洲城邦之间，依靠当地兵力与外交维持汉朝声威；他晚年上书请归，朝廷召还，经营西域的事业由后继者延续。
statement.en:
Ban Chao returned to Luoyang, was enfeoffed Marquis of Dingyuan, and soon died of illness aged 71. He had worked in the Western Regions for 31 years, winning over the oasis states by embassy, garrison farming and marriage ties, bringing more than fifty kingdoms to submit to the Eastern Han and reopening the Silk Road. With few officers and men he manoeuvred among the oasis cities, relying on local troops and diplomacy to uphold Han prestige; in old age he petitioned to return and the court recalled him, his work continuing under successors.

sources.excerpt: Its population has been estimated to be at least 25,000, but likely sat around 100,000 during its height, potentially making it the sixth-largest city in the world during its epoch.

en: From roughly AD 100 to 650, Teotihuacan in the Valley of Mexico developed into one of the largest cities in the Americas, with a peak population of about 125,000.

sources.excerpt: The urban grid had great significance to city planners when constructing Teotihuacan, as the cross is pecked into the ground in the Pyramid of the Sun in specific places throughout Teotihuacan in precise degrees and angles over three km in distance.

title.en: Rise of the Kingdom of Funan

summary.en: In the 1st-2nd centuries AD, the Kingdom of Funan (in modern Cambodia and southern Vietnam) rose in Southeast Asia. Funan was one of the earliest Indianized kingdoms in the region, controlling sea trade routes between India and China. Funan's ports were important transit points for East-West trade.

statement.zh: 公元1-2世纪，东南亚的扶南王国（Funan，今柬埔寨和越南南部）兴起。扶南是东南亚最早的印度化王国之一，控制着印度与中国之间的海上贸易路线。扶南的港口是东西方贸易的重要中转站。

title.en: Kingdom of Aksum rises

summary.en: The Aksumite kingdom of the Horn of Africa (modern Ethiopia) rose around the first century AD, commanding the Red Sea trade, minting its own gold and silver coins, and adopting Christianity as the state faith in the fourth century, a hinge between the classical world and the Indian Ocean.

title.en: Plutarch Wrote 'Parallel Lives'

summary.en: Around AD 100, the Greek historian Plutarch completed 'Parallel Lives' (Bioi parallēloi). The work pairs and compares famous Greek and Roman figures, covering a total of forty-six individuals. Plutarch's writings are among the most important sources for understanding ancient Greek and Roman history and were a major source of material for Shakespeare's plays.

statement.zh: 公元100年左右，希腊历史学家普鲁塔克（Plutarch）完成了《希腊罗马名人传》（Parallel Lives）。
statement.en: Around AD 100, the Greek historian Plutarch completed 'Parallel Lives' (Bioi parallēloi).
